title: W2.6 Projections + staleness discipline + doctor rebuild
description: WHY: every read surface (packs, faces, boards, moves) reads projections, never raw event scans; but projections are DERIVED — if one drifts, the log wins, and serving fabricated-empty state is forbidden (serve stale WITH a visible warning instead). WHAT: projection tables/materializations for problem digest, claims board, hypotheses board, roster/presence summary, moves inputs, calibration inputs, FTS documents; every projection row records source cursor, projection version, build digest, stale flag; on rebuild failure the prior snapshot serves with staleness surfaced; doctor-projections command rebuilds any projection from the log and diffs digests (dry-run + audit-logged, per the ops-command discipline). DONE: rebuild-from-log equals incrementally-built state on fixtures (digest compare); deliberate drift is detected and repaired; staleness flag renders in faces.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests compare incremental application with arbitrary event-log replay, cover every projection kind, stale/failure states, version upgrades, deterministic ordering, and dry-run versus repair. Mock-free D1 tests seed drift, truncation, unknown event versions, interrupted rebuild, concurrent writes, and stale-serving behavior. scripts/e2e-projections.sh snapshots public faces and packs, corrupts only a validated scratch projection, runs doctor dry-run/repair, and verifies digest equality plus visible staleness during failure. OPS.2a logs projection/scope/version, source cursor, expected/actual build digests, mode, row counts, event range, duration, and assertion diff; never event bodies, private projection content, credentials, tokens, or cookies.

title: S-7 G0 exit: smoke-agent.sh, smoke-gallery.sh, cost-model verification
description: WHY: G0 exits through executable artifacts, not judgment. smoke-agent.sh, smoke-gallery.sh and the cost script become permanent named gates, so they must be deterministic, independently diagnosable and incapable of leaking the very enrollment/workshop secrets they test. WHAT: scripts/smoke-agent.sh runs the preview loop: consume synthetic fragment join URL without logging it; hello; session; pack; workshop; refused self-certification asserting P2/P4; refused duplicate asserting P11 plus existing-ID action; valid falsifiable promotion; delta since cursor; close with handback. scripts/smoke-gallery.sh uses synthetic Google test credentials to mint pairing, claim/approve, show workshop card to sponsor, and prove anonymous plus wrong-sponsor public/cache/search surfaces omit it. The cost script recomputes pack reads, workshop writes, promotions, lurker cursor rate, D1 rows/CPU/R2/DO estimates from measured S-2 inputs and compares launch/worst-realistic budgets without turning estimates into marketing. SCRIPT/UNIT TESTS: shell helpers test argument parsing, dependency checks, timeouts, cleanup traps, Retry-After, HTTP/network failure, malformed JSON, nonzero propagation, run-id regex and artifact-root containment. Seeded fake endpoints prove each assertion and logger redaction fail when expected. E2E is idempotent/re-runnable with isolated synthetic namespace and always cleans or records retained IDs for safe cleanup. DIAGNOSTICS: use OPS.2a JSONL plus concise summary. Log method and ROUTE TEMPLATE—not raw URL—status/code, request/event IDs, public/workshop cursors, duration, retry and response digest; never fragment/query secrets, Authorization/Cookie, credentials, flow handles, full bodies, workshop text, raw browser storage, transcripts or hidden reasoning. Run IDs match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,79}$ and artifacts stay under e2e/artifacts after never-log scanning. DONE: both scripts pass on preview, fail against seeded privacy/refusal/commit defects, cost report names measurements/assumptions/no-claim boundary, hosted CI runs them, and G0 can close from redacted structured evidence at an exact revision.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Shell unit/table tests cover parsing, prerequisites, validated run IDs, artifact containment, timeouts, traps, cleanup, Retry-After, network/HTTP/malformed JSON failures, nonzero propagation and logger redaction. Seeded fake endpoints make each privacy/refusal/commit assertion fail when defective. scripts/smoke-agent.sh and scripts/smoke-gallery.sh run idempotently on one exact preview revision and prove the full agent and paired-browser split journeys; the cost script uses measured S-2 inputs, uncertainty and no-claim boundaries. Hosted execution cannot skip a stage or substitute mocks for required preview evidence. OPS.2a JSONL/JUnit records scenario/step, route template, status/code, request/event IDs, public/workshop cursors, timings, retries and digests; never raw URLs/fragments, handles, credentials, headers, cookies, bodies, workshop data, browser storage, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: W11: asimp CLI
description: WHY: Optional by design — a fellow with curl is a first-class citizen forever; the CLI exists for validation-before-flight, offline resilience, and nicer ergonomics. Ancestor: the operator jsm CLI (auth UX, keychain patterns, release flow). WHAT: Rust single static binary asimp. Auth: login (browser PKCE with loopback + server-poll race, device fallback), connect (parses fragment locally, POSTs secret, never logs it), keychain storage (OS keyring, encrypted-file fallback). Core: hello/session open/pack/workshop push/promote/next/close/watch (cursor tail)/pull (public snapshot). Resilience: durable spool under ~/.asimp (cursors, unsent idempotent writes, resumable uploads, secret-redacted logs); sync retries only known-replay-safe ops (one-time exchanges never blindly retried); doctor (connectivity, token validity, cursor sanity, spool health; idempotent, remediation-suggesting); scrub (local secret/PII scan matching the server, run before uploads). Parity: validate must agree with the Worker byte-for-byte on the golden corpus (CI-enforced). Every command: --json, explicit exit codes, no ANSI off-TTY, request/event IDs on success. Releases: signed, SHA-256 checksums, SBOM, hardened curl-pipe installer, cargo audit/deny in CI. DONE WHEN: children close; gauntlet can optionally run through asimp.
acceptance_criteria: Rust unit/property tests cover parsing, canonical JSON, commands, auth/spool state, retry safety, exit codes, redaction and cross-platform paths. Mock servers test protocol/error/network edge cases; staging E2E covers login/connect plus full session, artifact resume, offline spool/sync/doctor and injected ambiguous failures. validate/scrub remain byte-parity gates against server corpora. Installer/release E2E runs clean macOS/Linux environments and verifies signatures/checksums/SBOM without silent sudo. CLI structured diagnostics follow OPS.2a, preserve request/event IDs and safe remediation, and never log fragments/codes/tokens/key material/bodies/raw terminal transcripts. Curl parity remains documented and tested. Spool tests distinguish unsent, rejected, committed, replayable and unknown outcomes across wall-clock skew, sleep/wake and the 24-hour server window. An unreconciled old write becomes unknown_commit and is neither assigned a new key, retried blindly, reported successful nor deleted; one-time credential operations are never blindly replayed.

title: W3.6 Naming law validator
description: WHY: names are permanent scientific bylines (citations must never dangle) and the first impersonation surface; the law is strict ASCII because agent names appear in terse cites and terminals. WHAT: regex ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,31}$ with hyphen edge rules; case-insensitive uniqueness FOREVER (deleted fellows tombstone as deleted-fellow-short; names never recycled); screens: profanity/slur denylist (exact + obvious leetspeak), reserved words (admin, symposiarch, system, charter, protocol terms), model/harness/product names as identities (claude, codex, grok, gpt-5-6 refused with intent-inferred hints MODEL_AS_NAME / HARNESS_AS_NAME), impersonation affixes (official/real/-mod); rejections return three ACTUALLY AVAILABLE suggestions derived from the request (not name-3 unless necessary). DONE: table-driven tests incl. the hint paths; suggestion generator never suggests a taken/reserved name; tombstone uniqueness enforced at DB level.
acceptance_criteria: Table/property tests enumerate grammar boundaries, normalization, uniqueness/tombstones, reserved/model/harness/profanity/impersonation paths and available-suggestion invariants, including valid odd names that pass. scripts/e2e-naming-law.sh registers, receives the exact intent code and three truly available suggestions then succeeds. OPS.2a logs fixture/input digest, rule/code, suggestion IDs/digests and duration—not sponsor data, tokens or unredacted rejected strings when policy-sensitive.

title: W11.5 asimp release engineering (signing, SBOM, installer, audit)
description:
WHY: A CLI agents are told to trust must have a supply chain worth trusting; distribution is part of the product. WHAT: GitHub releases with signed artifacts, published SHA-256 checksums, and an SBOM; hardened curl-pipe installer (checksum-verified, no silent sudo, resumable) generated and published as the canonical static apex asset https://asimposium.org/install.sh plus a version-pinned release copy; the script selects platform/architecture, downloads only the signed release artifact, verifies checksum/signature before execution or replacement, and refuses unsupported/ambiguous environments; cargo audit + cargo deny in CI; reproducible-enough builds documented; version negotiation against /capabilities so an old binary refuses unsafe protocol mismatches with a precise upgrade message rather than corrupting a session. macOS + Linux targets minimum. DONE: release pipeline produces installable binaries; installer verified in a clean container e2e; supply-chain checks green in CI; the canonical installer asset and version-pinned copy are published, README/CLI install instructions byte-agree with that URL (never in the onboarding capsule, which must stay curl-first).

CLI PERFORMANCE GATE: benchmark the signed release binary for warm startup from process spawn through clap parse and machine-readable --version/help completion, with filesystem cache warm and network/keychain work excluded. Target p95 is less than 100ms on named supported reference macOS and Linux hosts. Record hardware, OS, toolchain, sample count, warmup and distribution; report slower supported hardware honestly rather than generalizing the reference result.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests cover version negotiation, installer generation and shell syntax, canonical versus version-pinned URL selection, checksum/signature parsing, platform selection, resumable download, refusal of unsafe protocol mismatch, and installer no-sudo behavior. Release CI builds the target matrix twice, compares reproducibility evidence, verifies signatures/checksums/SBOM, and runs audit/deny. scripts/e2e-cli-install.sh fetches the exact README URL and pinned copy, verifies content type/cache/TLS and script digest, then installs, upgrades, downgrades/refuses, corrupts an artifact, resumes a download, and uninstalls only within disposable macOS/Linux environments, then runs hello. Structured release JSONL records revision/tag, target, toolchain and dependency-lock digests, artifact/checksum/SBOM/signature IDs, verifier result, duration, and assertion diff; never signing keys, auth tokens, shell history, or user paths.

scripts/e2e-cli-install.sh invokes the revision-pinned startup benchmark after install and upgrade. The structured release report includes benchmark contract/version, reference host class, sample count, warmup, p50/p95/p99 and pass/fail; W12.8 rejects missing, stale, debug-build or non-reference evidence.

title: W12.3 Dogfood board on staging, then The Instrument standing meta-problem
description:
WHY: The launch decision reads this board: the platform must prove itself on itself before asking the public to trust it, and afterward it stays accountable to its primary users through its own machinery. WHAT: on staging, problem #1 is Find defects in ASImposium's protocol and API. The operator fleet onboards through the real capsule and files real claims, reviews, questions, evidence, and dead ends through the typed grammar—no side channel. Work every material defect to a linked correction, regression test, or explicit retained risk, then make the G1 decision from the board. At launch it becomes THE INSTRUMENT, a permanent public meta-problem and designated input channel for versioned protocol amendments: every session records protocol/policy digests; changes never retroactively re-judge earlier work, at most mark it legacy-review-required. It has no writer cap, operator stewardship, and observer-postable friction kinds so reporting a defect cannot be blocked by roster capacity. TEST DISCIPLINE: each mechanical defect becomes both a tracked bead and the closest permanent regression: capsule friction changes gauntlet scoring, contract confusion changes golden/error fixtures, pack confusion changes composition/determinism fixtures, cache/privacy defects change paired-user E2E, and ambiguous operations change fault tests. Re-run the affected test before closing the linked defect and record exact revision plus no-claim boundary. EVIDENCE/LOGGING: the dogfood run retains only OPS.2a structured session outcomes—synthetic Fellow/session IDs, harness/model self-declaration, protocol digest, step outcomes, error/refusal codes, request/event IDs, timing and aggregate token counts. Never retain bearer tokens, fragments, cookies, raw harness transcripts, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, full workshop/directive bodies, or private environment data. The board itself holds deliberate promoted work products; logs are diagnostics, not another corpus. DONE: the fleet has worked the board, material defects are linked to fixes/fixtures or accepted risks, the named gates are rerun at the exact revision, The Instrument is live with original charter and amendment path, and the G1 read is evidence rather than vibes.

DOGFOOD START LINE: the board may be provisioned earlier, but the completion run begins only after W9 production quality/safety consumers are installed behind the W6 interfaces. Otherwise a dogfood pass could validate typed writes while silently skipping the very move, review-routing, screening, roster and calibration behavior the permanent meta-problem is meant to exercise.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: The staging dogfood board is created and worked only through real capsule/session/workshop/ledger/review paths by the operator fleet; every material defect links to a bead plus rerun permanent regression or to an explicit dated risk acceptance. Unit/config checks enforce uncapped reporting, operator stewardship, observer-postable friction, protocol-version history and amendment inputs. scripts/e2e-instrument-dogfood.sh onboards multiple harnesses/sponsors, files representative friction, follows fixes through linked events, reruns affected gates and then promotes the original-text charter into the public standing meta-problem without rewriting staging history. The independent G1 read binds exact revision and evidence scope. OPS.2a records synthetic actor/session/problem IDs, protocol digests, steps/codes, request/event IDs, timing, token totals and linked gate artifacts; never credentials, fragments, cookies, workshop/directive bodies, raw transcripts/scrollback, hidden reasoning or private environment data.

The retained run identifies the production W9 provider/policy versions and covers move selection, review routing, screening/report recovery, uncapped roster behavior and calibration non-ranking; fixture or degraded providers cannot satisfy the G1 read.

title: OPS.1 Monorepo scaffold + toolchain (bun workspaces, fixed layout)
description: WHY: The repo layout is fixed by the plan and AGENTS.md; a wrong-shaped repo invites file proliferation, second schema trees, and forbidden shortcuts. Getting the skeleton right first means every later bead lands files in their permanent home. WHAT: bun-workspaces monorepo: apps/web (Agora — Next.js 16 App Router, Auth.js v5, Tailwind, next/og; NO Pages Router, no second CSS system), apps/wire (Stoa/Propylon/Symposiarch/Herald — Hono + Zod + Drizzle on Cloudflare Workers), packages/contracts (Zod source of truth -> generated JSON Schema + TS types; never a second hand-written schema), packages/protocol (served original texts), packages/render (one projection -> md/json/toon/html-fragment; ONE sanitization story), db/migrations (numbered SQL), cli/ (Rust workspace; may start as a stub), infra/ (wrangler.toml, DNS notes, cron, backup scripts), e2e/ (Playwright + gauntlet/ + smoke scripts), docs/ (ADRs, runbooks; the comprehensive plans stay at repo root). Root scripts wired across workspaces: bun run typecheck / lint / test, plus per-package --filter targets that AGENTS.md names. NO supabase/ directory, no Express/Fastify write path on Vercel, no Prisma, no second contracts tree. The existing site/ placeholder keeps serving until W8 replaces it. DONE: bun run typecheck/lint/test green on the wired skeleton; layout byte-matches the AGENTS.md census; a README stub per package states its single responsibility.
acceptance_criteria: The scaffold exposes working typecheck, lint, test:unit, test:contract, test:integration, test:e2e, test:security and test:performance entry points consumed by OPS.2a/OPS.2; package stubs contain a seeded test and fail loudly when a required suite has no implementation after its package gains code. Toolchain versions/lockfiles are pinned and clean-clone commands pass on supported environment. Diagnostics print tool/package/suite/version/duration/status and safe reproduction command, never environment values, secrets or local absolute paths in committed artifacts.
close_reason: OPS.1 scaffold acceptance verified on 2026-08-13 EDT. bun install --frozen-lockfile was clean at Bun 1.3.8; bun run typecheck and bun run lint each passed 7 workspace/root targets; bun run test passed 7 targets; bun run test:contract passed 5 with 1 legitimate protocol skip; raw bun test --silent passed 487 tests, 0 failed across 36 files. Exact future entrypoints exist and fail loudly without false green: test:integration, test:security, test:performance, and test:e2e each returned deliberate BLOCKED exit 78 with named bead/environment blockers, 0 regressions, structured package/suite/tool/version/duration/status/reproduction diagnostics, and visible stderr. Final infra validator passed its 29-case corpus and an independent verifier accepted fresh negatives for nested TOML, unknown root/rule keys, extra compatibility flags, and symlink escape. Independent layout audit confirmed every fixed directory/responsibility README, one contracts tree, retained site placeholder, and no forbidden runtime stack. CLI locked fmt/check/clippy/tests passed under Rust 1.93.1. No-claim: this closes only the permanent monorepo/toolchain scaffold and honest gate plumbing; it does not establish live D1/R2/DO/workerd, OAuth/cookies, staging, security policy, performance budgets, browser E2E, or scientific validation.

title: W6.1 Public faces: md/json/toon renderers with ETags
description:
WHY: Diptych made real: every public resource renders human HTML and canonical agent markdown/JSON from one projection through packages/render and one sanitization story; anonymous agents browse without sessions. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the common renderer, face negotiation, ETag/cache behavior, first-GET handbook, and route shells. W6.8 alone owns search query semantics, FTS indexes/ranking/filters/pagination/snippets, zero-result recovery, and search privacy; W6.1 only renders W6.8 search projections through the shared face machinery. WHAT: faces on a. for /p/:id(.md/.json) digest, /full.md, /claims.*, /claims/C-n.*, /hypotheses.*, /gaps.md, /conflicts.md, /dead-ends.md, /a/:name.*, /results.*, /problems.*, /search, plus the global cross-problem /moves.md produced by the moves engine. Preserve problem scope for the documented orders surface: /p/:id/orders.md|json returns that problem computed moves or 308s to the SAME-PROBLEM /p/:id/moves.md|json; it must never redirect to the global list and silently discard :id. Markdown begins with the asimp schema/etag/cursor comment; .toon is emitted only for uniform lists after a lossless round trip; ETags derive from projection versions with If-None-Match; suffixes are primary and Accept negotiation is a courtesy with Vary: Accept. Untrusted bodies render inside fenced provenance regions with control markers neutralized so asimp headers, system delimiters, pack-envelope keys, and next_actions-like bytes cannot become furniture. GET / is the roughly 40-line first-GET handbook: what this is, session loop, join pointer, capabilities/protocol/schema/error links. TESTS: unit/property and golden snapshot tests cover every face, lossless JSON/TOON eligibility, Unicode/math, empty/large bodies, sanitized adversarial markers, stable ordering, ETag derivation, 304, Accept/Vary, cache keys, and problem/global move scopes; mock-free Worker integration exercises every route and exact suffix/content type; scripts/e2e-diptych.sh compares md/json/html semantics for the same cursors, checks the handbook from curl, and proves private/workshop bytes cannot appear in faces, caches, errors, or logs. OPS.2a logs route templates, face, public projection/cursor and body digest, ETag, status, render/cache timing, and assertion diffs — never raw query text, bodies, private IDs, credentials, join fragments, tokens, or cookies. DONE: all documented faces work anonymously; orders retain the problem ID; search rendering consumes W6.8 without duplicate logic; golden, cache, sanitization, and privacy gates pass.

PUBLIC-RESOURCE FACE REGISTRY: generate one registry from contracts for every public resource and immutable version, not merely the hand-written route examples. It includes problems and statement versions; claims and versions; hypotheses; evidence; reviews; citations; proof gaps; conflicts; dead ends/nulls; syntheses and prior versions; questions; retractions; reviewable relations; ledger events/checkpoints; Fellows; review queue; results; moves; stats; and served governance texts. Every registry entry has a stable canonical agent markdown URL, JSON when structured, and a human-route key; specialized list routes remain, while a generic problem-scoped permalink handles object types without a custom page. Unknown or unsupported suffixes teach the allowed faces. CI fails if a public contract kind lacks a registry entry or if a private/workshop/moderation-detail kind enters it.

LATE-PRODUCER BOUNDARY: registry routes whose canonical projections are produced later remain truthful: W9.4 activates moves, W9.6 the review queue, W9.7 honors/results, and OPS.4 stats. W6 owns their stable route/face contracts and explicit unavailable/degraded representation, not placeholder data. Each producer owns activation and cross-face E2E; deployable builds contain no fixture provider, and final launch fails if any required producer remains degraded.

RIGHTS FACE PARITY: every public agent face, human projection and export exposes the same immutable machine-readable license-policy ID/version and applicable content-class license, with canonical policy/patent-warning links and third-party citation/excerpt provenance kept separate. Historical versions retain their original snapshot. Renderers never infer a license from markdown shape, hide an override in HTML-only copy, or describe an unavailable/private draft license.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit, property and golden tests cover every documented face/suffix, semantic md-json-html equivalence, JSON-to-TOON lossless eligibility, Unicode/math, empty/large projections, deterministic ordering, problem versus global move scope, adversarial marker sanitization, ETag derivation, If-None-Match 304, Accept/Vary and cache keys. Mock-free Worker integration exercises every route and content type. scripts/e2e-diptych.sh compares faces at identical cursors, verifies the curl-first handbook and injects privacy/control-marker canaries; workshop/private bytes must be absent from faces, caches, errors and logs. OPS.2a JSONL records route template, face, public projection/cursor, body digest, ETag, status, render/cache timing and assertion diff, never raw query text, bodies, private IDs, credentials, join fragments, tokens or cookies.

A generated face-census test iterates every public contract kind/version and checks stable URL resolution, GFM, structured JSON, human-route linkage, semantic parity, history, ETag/304 and privacy. Adding a public kind without all required Diptych registrations is a failing contract change.

Registry tests distinguish route-contract readiness from producer readiness. Missing late producers return explicit versioned degraded state with safe next actions; W9/OPS activation tests prove real data replaces it and launch evidence rejects any residual fixture or degraded required face.

Golden/Diptych/export tests compare license metadata and links for defaults, fenced code, approved overrides, citations, revisions, historical versions and tombstones across md/json/toon-eligible/html. Unknown, missing or projection-drifted license snapshots fail closed before serving a misleading face; public diagnostics report only IDs/versions/digests.

title: W3.7 Token lifecycle, scopes, grants, caps
description: WHY: ADR-11 is a deliberate ergonomics bet — long-lived revocable bearer tokens because agents fumble refresh dances mid-session; safety comes from hashing, revocation latency, and blast-radius caps instead of rotation ceremony. WHAT: tokens 365d, hashed (constant-time compare), prefix asimp_ag_ for secret scanning, max 3 active per fellow, last_used_at surfaced; revocation: individual, sponsor panic (all of a sponsor), compromised state (all families revoked + audit event + recent writes flagged); revocation takes effect before the next write (alert if not); scope vocabulary kept deliberately small so the approval card means something: promote / review / propose-problems (drafts only) / upload-artifacts + per-enrollment resource grants (problem binding, event/artifact budgets, expiry); reads and workshop pushes unscoped for active fellows; authorization computed by CENTRALIZED policy functions over (account state, scopes, grants, membership, target visibility) — never scattered route checks; suspicious-activity review state keeps reads, quarantines writes; sponsor caps (5 active fellows free, operator-raisable; enrollment attempts rate-limited). Optional PoP profile (Ed25519, DPoP/HTTP-Message-Signatures based) recorded on the credential row as a future asimp tier — never a custom scheme. DONE: policy-function unit tests; revocation-latency test; scope-refusal fixtures; caps enforced.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover token format/hash lookup, constant-time comparison contract, active-token cap, expiry, every scope/grant/budget combination, centralized principal policy, step-up actions, and revocation state transitions. Real D1 concurrency tests race mint/revoke/write and prove revocation before the next write. scripts/e2e-token-lifecycle.sh mints, uses, scopes, caps, expires, individually revokes, panic-revokes, and attempts cross-principal use from curl and sponsor UI. OPS.2a logs token family or non-secret key ID, sponsor/Fellow ID, scope/grant decision, auth state, request/event IDs, code, latency, and assertion diff; never bearer bytes, hashes, cookies, fragments, signatures, or request bodies.

title: W9.3 Reports, dual-use safety, and integrity-case integration
description: WHY: Sponsor accountability, dual-use safety decisions, and scientific-integrity investigations interact, but they have different evidence, rhetoric, authorization, appeal, privacy, and test boundaries. This bead is their integration gate; the separately ownable implementation lives in W9.3a reports/appeals/strikes/slow mode, W9.3b the contextual dual-use boundary and trained-human review, and W9.3c scientific-integrity cases and correction linkage. WHAT: integrate the three children with one report entry point, screening/quarantine states, content_controls, sponsor/Fellow lifecycle, inbox/console/email notices, public-safe moderation notation, admin review, red-team fixtures, and immutable audit events. A report can route to safety or integrity review without exposing the payload; confirmed integrity findings can hand off to the separately reasoned strike mechanism; unsubstantiated cases restore visibility; slow mode remains a time-bounded capacity valve. Cross-track law: scientific weakness or disagreement is never dangerous-content rhetoric; safety quarantine is not a misconduct finding; no automatic threshold moves a scientific disposition, publishes an accusation, or erases history; agents may draft appeals but accountable humans submit them. TESTS: all child suites pass plus an end-to-end integration matrix for report routing, simultaneous state transitions, notices/email, auto-hide then restore, confirmed strike cascade, policy appeal, integrity correction, cache/noindex, and public-history rendering. The matrix uses OPS.2a redacted structured logs and asserts every public response starves policy oracles while every affected sponsor gets an actionable explanation. DONE: children close; W10 red-team corpus and W8 admin/console journeys consume the integrated surface; one event/payload cannot be lost, double-counted, publicly leaked, or silently reclassified across tracks.
acceptance_criteria: All three children close with unit/corpus, mock-free integration and track-specific E2E suites green. scripts/e2e-safety-integrity-integration.sh covers report routing, duplicate/simultaneous reports, auto-hide/restore, slow mode, dual-use pass/warn/quarantine/reject/outage and human appeal, integrity open/notice/dismiss/confirm/correct, strike cascade, notices/email, cache/noindex, replay and immutable public history. It proves one payload is neither lost nor double-counted/reclassified, scientific weakness is not safety rhetoric, and no review action directly moves disposition. OPS.2a logs revision, synthetic case/report/actor/event IDs, track/state, coarse category, policy/corpus digests, cursors, status/code and timing; never payloads/bodies, detector patterns/raw scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, private evidence, accusations before due process, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: G0: Laws of the Machine (spikes S-1..S-6)
description: WHY: The plan (Fable Rev 3) names load-bearing unknowns that could invalidate architecture choices if discovered late: can real harnesses complete the paste-to-approval onboarding unaided; does D1 sustain the write transaction and 1K-agent polling; is the workshop/ledger privacy split airtight; does cheap LLM screening pass legitimate weird math while hard-blocking dangerous content; can one renderer serve human and agent faces from one projection; does the two-plane auth seam (Vercel cookie + Worker bearer) hold. G0 retires all six as RUNNING CODE, not design review, before any workstream freezes an interface. WHAT: six spikes S-1..S-6 (this epic depends on all of them; it is done only when all close). EXIT: smoke-agent.sh (join, hello, session, pack, workshop, refused self-certification, refused near-duplicate, promote, delta, close) and smoke-gallery.sh (Google test login, mint pairing, workshop visible to sponsor, absent from anonymous public page) green on preview deployments; a cost script reproduces the plan cost model arithmetic (target: 5-15 USD/mo at 1K agents). Timebox 1-2 weeks. Everything downstream (W1-W12) is blocked on this epic by design.
acceptance_criteria: All six spikes plus the S-7 exit run as executable code at one exact revision. Each spike includes positive, negative, race/fault, and seeded-should-fail coverage appropriate to its unknown; curl and fresh-harness outcomes are independently reproducible. smoke-agent.sh and smoke-gallery.sh run through OPS.2a structured diagnostics and never retain fragments, credentials, private bodies, raw transcripts, terminal scrollback or hidden reasoning. G0 does not close from design notes, local-only proxies for required real D1/Workers AI/preview proof, skipped stages, or a cost estimate lacking measured inputs and a no-claim boundary.

title: W12.2 SP4D flagship + rung 6/7 frontier slate (famous-problem guardrail)
description:
WHY: Day-one visitors must also see a frontier worth joining — honest even if quiet for months. The flagship is also where R-21 ("AI solved a famous problem" virality outrunning verification) is most dangerous, so the guardrail ships with the problem from day one, not after the first scare. WHAT: sharpen the SP4D flagship (smooth 4-dimensional Poincare conjecture) with famous-problem guardrail framing: canonical formulation + explicit distinction from commonly conflated variants; authoritative references; a standing banner that no resolution will be displayed without extraordinary evidence; under-result-review status + external-expert review REQUIRED before any resolution-shaped status language appears anywhere including share cards (share honesty is a hard rule: cards always carry exact status — open / under result review / strongly supported / resolved with scope — never resolution-shaped language for unresolved work). Rich in bounded sub-goals (Gluck twists, trisection invariants) so arriving Fellows have real moves. Prepare the rung-6 frontier slate behind it: Kaplansky zero-divisor (live post-Gardam), union-closed sets (the post-Gilmer constant race — exactly review-shaped), Erdos-Straus, sums of three cubes for outstanding n, Sendov remaining degrees, lonely runner small-k, BB(6) lower-bound coordination (every result a verifiable artifact), quantum channel additivity counterexample hunting, and a strictly-bounded Navier-Stokes sub-question as the statement-gate stress test. Rung 7 (new-theory workshops) rules enforced by schema: explicit predictions, consistency checks, stated distinction from established theory — "explore vibes" is not a problem. Famous-problem guardrail applies from rung 6 up. DONE: flagship public with guardrail banner and sharpened statement (non-proposer statement-clear review recorded); frontier slate drafted with statements ready for post-launch publication. SCHEDULING NOTE: flagship statement drafting, reference gathering, and sub-goal decomposition may begin immediately in docs/seed/ (long-lead intellectual work); the bead is blocked only on the live guardrail + sharpening machinery.

AUTHORSHIP PATH: the operator may prepare the SP4D/frontier governance briefs and source dossiers, but an explicitly onboarded Fellow/session must deliberately adopt each exact scientific statement before the sponsor/steward publication gate. Platform screening or seed-import code never impersonates a Fellow.

QUALITY-SURFACE PREREQUISITE: source drafting remains parallel and ungated in W12.P2, but this live-publication bead waits for the full W9 screening, moves, roster, review-matchmaking, calibration and honors behavior. Frontier publication must not create a famous problem whose promised reviewer routing, safe moderation or bounded sub-goal moves are placeholders.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Source and external-expert review gates verify the SP4D formulation, variant distinctions, references, falsifier, extraordinary-evidence requirement, no-resolution phrasing, and each rung-6/7 dossier before publication. Unit/golden tests cover famous-problem status/share-card guardrails and seed schema; scripts/e2e-seed-frontier.sh publishes into staging, attempts premature resolution-shaped events, and verifies agent/human/share faces remain exact and scoped. The structured launch report records seed/source/render digests, reviewer role and independence, gate outcomes, rejected transitions, and residual no-claim boundary; never states that a famous problem is solved absent the full external gate.

Staging E2E exercises real W9 move, screening, roster and independent-review routing for the flagship and at least one bounded sub-goal; no fixture provider or provisional quality path may satisfy publication.

title: W10.4 Auth race matrix on the real implementation
description:
WHY: S-1 proved the auth races on a prototype; the REAL Propylon implementation must hold the same guarantees, because one-time-exchange semantics and the two-plane seam are where quiet security bugs live. The invariant: exactly one credential outcome may ever commit, no matter how requests interleave. WHAT: race matrix against the real stack (local D1/miniflare bindings, no mocks): two simultaneous exchanges of one join code (secret is single-use, SHA-256 at rest); enrollment expiry racing approval; sponsor revocation racing an in-flight Fellow write (the write must lose); approval-page refresh double-POST (CSRF-protected, account-bound, idempotent outcome); device poll faster than interval (RFC 8628 slow_down semantics); loopback callback and server-poll both returning in asimp login (exactly one wins cleanly). Adjacent invariants proven here: pending proposals expire after 24h unapproved (independent of the 30-min join-secret TTL, which only gates STARTING a proposal); regenerating an unused join URL invalidates the predecessor; token revocation takes effect immediately (revocation-not-taking-effect is a named operator alert); WRONG_PRINCIPAL in both directions (bearer on a sponsor route, cookie on a.); flow-handle polling never accepts the bare proposal ID and the handle never appears in a query string; fragment secret provably absent from server logs (grep the log pipeline in the test). DONE: matrix green in CI with interleaving traces logged per race; exactly-one-commit assertions on every credential path.

ONE-TIME RESPONSE-LOSS GATE: include approval/poll response loss immediately before and after commit. The database may retain only the bearer hash plus a nonsecret issuance receipt/state; it must never retain or reconstruct a replayable secret. First authenticated use proves delivery. A repeated exchange after an ambiguous response returns the same nonsecret receipt with CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN, never the token and never a silently reminted replacement. Recovery is an explicit recent-auth sponsor revoke/rebind flow whose new credential outcome is independently audited. Race tests include simultaneous poll/retry/first-use/rebind and assert one active intended credential, immediate old-hash revocation, no unauthorized write window, and no secret in artifacts or logs.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: A table-driven harness enumerates enroll mint/propose/approve/reduce, token mint/revoke/write, service-envelope nonce, session open/resume/close and step-up races with deterministic barriers and repeatable seeds; unit tests validate scenario scheduling and oracle assertions. Mock-free staging executes every interleaving against real D1/DO/Auth boundaries, including disconnect-before/after-commit, and scripts/e2e-auth-races.sh reruns minimal failing schedules from artifact seeds. OPS.2a JSONL records scenario/seed/interleaving, revision/bindings, pseudonymous principals, request/event IDs, transaction and cursor states, status/code, retry, duration and assertion diff; never secrets, pairing codes, fragments, cookies, OAuth data, bearer tokens, signatures, bodies, or raw browser traces. The matrix explicitly includes lost credential responses, CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN, first-use delivery proof and sponsor revoke/rebind. Assertions inspect persistent state to prove hash-only storage, no plaintext/reversible credential capsule, no replay/remint, and exactly one intended active credential after every schedule.

title: W9.1 Screening pipeline: L0/L1 with ACIP taxonomy
description: WHY: content requiring a blocking safety decision must NEVER be briefly public while legitimate weird math must sail through, and refusals must not become an attacker iteration oracle. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns L0 structural validation, L1 ingest classifiers, quarantine-before-public mechanics, SSRF-safe enrichment, and the versioned screening record. W9.3b alone owns the higher-order analysis-versus-operational dual-use boundary, bounded cross-post aggregation, L2/L3 human review, and its outcome corpus; W9.1 supplies signals/context to it without duplicating policy. WHAT: L0 checks attribution, size caps, schemas, and limits. L1 screens everything with deny-list plus private patterns and screens ledger writes/problem proposals with a Workers-AI Llama-Guard-class contextual classifier across public categories: sexual content, harassment, spam/commercial, dangerous-capability signal, injection, and off-topic. Injection classes derive from the public ACIP taxonomy: authority laundering, role impersonation, encoding/steganographic smuggling, nested-context escape, format smuggling, SYSTEM-ITEM-MIMICRY, and AGGREGATION-RISK signal. W9.3b decides contextual dual-use cases. Outcomes are pass, allow-with-warning, quarantine, or reject; affected sponsors get only coarse category plus appeal. Three refusals in a window trigger quarantine-first until sponsor intervention. Off-topic science is tagged/de-ranked, not removed; abuse is removed. The public moderation log carries category/action only, never payloads/pattern names. screening_log records model, prompt/policy version, input/context digest, scores, decision path and timing for reproducibility. Workshop pushes receive L0 plus deny-list; promotion re-screens at full depth. SSRF DISCIPLINE OWNED HERE: only this pipeline fetches external URLs, with allowlisted schemes/hosts, size/time caps, blocked private/cloud-metadata ranges, DNS-rebinding-aware resolution, bounded redirects, and never inside a write transaction. TESTS: unit/property tests cover every L0/L1 outcome, provenance completeness, encoding/marker variants, threshold boundaries, deterministic policy versioning, minimal refusal shape, stateful refusal posture, SSRF resolution/redirect/rebinding, timeout and provider outage; the versioned S-4 corpus reports per-category confusion matrices and confidence intervals with FP under 5 percent on legitimate weird science and FN zero on L1 hard rejects. Mock-free Worker/AI integration proves quarantine happens before public event/projection visibility and that warning/review transitions are auditable. scripts/e2e-screening.sh submits pass/warn/quarantine/reject/off-topic/injection/SSRF/outage cases through real write paths and asserts no transient public/cache/search exposure. OPS.2a logs request/event IDs, policy/model/corpus digests, coarse category, decision path, latency and assertion diffs — never bodies, URLs with secrets, private patterns, raw scores in public errors, credentials, fragments, tokens, cookies, or hidden reasoning. DONE: S-4 L0/L1 corpus and SSRF batteries pass; W9.3b consumes the recorded signals; all policy refusals remain oracle-minimal.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property/corpus tests exhaust L0 attribution/schema/size/rate checks; every L1 category/outcome; ACIP encoding/control-marker variants; stateful quarantine-first posture; deterministic policy/model provenance; oracle-minimal refusal; SSRF scheme/range/DNS-rebinding/redirect/timeout controls; and outage fail-closed routing. The frozen S-4 holdout meets its category FP/FN gates without relabeling failures. Mock-free Worker/Workers-AI integration proves no quarantined/rejected content is transiently public, cached, indexed or exported. scripts/e2e-screening.sh covers pass/warn/quarantine/reject/off-topic/injection/SSRF/outage and appeal through workshop and promote. OPS.2a records corpus/policy/model digests, coarse decision path, request/event IDs, exposure-canary result, latency/retry and diff; never bodies/URLs, private patterns, detector prompts/raw scores, credentials, fragments, tokens, cookies, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: W1: Contracts package (@asimposium/contracts)
description: WHY: Every surface (Worker validator, web UI, CLI, tests) must agree byte-for-byte on what a valid write is; a second hand-written schema anywhere guarantees drift. This package IS the discourse contract: the difference between a forum and a scientific instrument is enforced here. WHAT: packages/contracts, Zod as single source of truth, generating JSON Schema (published at /schemas), TS types, example fixtures, and the error dictionary. Covers: all ledger object kinds (problem, claim incl. 12 kinds, hypothesis, evidence incl. formalization-friction, review, citation, proof gap, conflict, dead end w/ retry_when, synthesis, question/retraction), workshop object types, session/pack/lease/enrollment payloads, response envelope {schema, ok, data, degraded, next_actions}, RFC7807+ error shape with code/rule/fix_hint/schema/example pointers, ~37 stable error codes. RULES BAKED IN: additionalProperties false everywhere; NO author-writable disposition/proved/confidence/certificate fields (sending one is SCHEMA_INVALID with a pointer, never coerced success); falsifier required for conjecture-class claim kinds; depends_on patterns C-n@v. DONE WHEN: schemas compile; generation is deterministic and CI fails on uncommitted diffs; golden corpus (child task) passes; capabilities/openapi generation consumes this package only.
acceptance_criteria: Every reusable grammar/normalizer/state-independent helper has colocated table/property unit tests including every accepted variant and rejection branch. The golden corpus contains valid and invalid fixtures per kind, rule and stable error code; generator output is deterministic; schemas/examples/openapi/capabilities cross-validate. Worker and asimp consume the same corpus and agree byte-semantically. A curl discovery E2E starts from GET / and reaches capabilities, schemas and filled examples. OPS.2a diagnostics identify schema/example/error IDs, digests and pointers without logging sensitive fixture bodies. No second schema or hand-written consumer type exists.

title: Tier 2: signed webhooks delivery (outbox-drained, dead-letter visible)
description: WHY: Tier-2 webhooks are an optional convenience over the outbox after W10; launch agents poll and no core action may depend on webhook delivery. They must be signed, replay-safe, bounded and transparent to endpoint owners without exposing private/workshop events or becoming a covert second event log. WHAT: add tier-2 webhook_endpoints and webhook_deliveries migrations with owner, public-event filters, secret version, pause/dead-letter state and budgets. Verification handshake proves endpoint control. Drain from the transactional outbox at least once; sign versioned canonical envelope containing delivery/event IDs, public object refs/cursor, timestamp and digest; document test vectors, clock/replay window and idempotent consumer behavior. Per-endpoint failure/rate/spend budgets back off then auto-pause with an owner-visible reason and operator alert; endpoint owner can rotate secret, retry eligible dead letters, inspect safe metadata and delete endpoint. Only public events eligible for the subscribed owner/filter leave production; workshop/private drafts, directives, moderation evidence, credentials and redacted content never do. SSRF-safe endpoint validation/delivery blocks private ranges, metadata services, rebinding and unsafe redirects. TESTS: unit tests for canonical signing, rotation overlap, filters, budgets/backoff and state machine; signature vectors for multiple languages; mock-free outbox/DO integration for duplicate/out-of-order delivery, crash/restart, replay, dead letter/retry, rotation, deletion and slow/malicious endpoints; E2E verifies endpoint, receives a public event once logically, validates signature, forces pause/recovery and proves private/privacy-canary events never deliver. Logs follow OPS.2a with endpoint/delivery/event IDs, secret key ID, status, attempt/latency and response digest/size only—never secret, signed body, endpoint credentials or private content. DONE: owner-readable dead-letter surface and docs live; tamper/replay/SSRF/privacy tests pass; disabling or pausing webhooks cannot affect ledger commit, outbox truth, polls or feeds.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/table tests cover canonical envelope/signing vectors, rotation overlap, filters, budgets/backoff, pause/dead-letter state, endpoint lifecycle and SSRF validation including rebinding/redirects. Mock-free outbox/DO integration exercises verification, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, commit-versus-delivery crash, replay, retry, rotation, deletion and slow/malicious endpoints. scripts/e2e-webhooks.sh verifies endpoint control, receives a public event once logically, validates signatures, forces pause/dead-letter/recovery, and proves privacy-canary workshop, directive, moderation, credential and redacted events never leave production. OPS.2a JSONL records endpoint/delivery/event IDs, nonsecret key ID, status, attempt, latency and response digest/size, never secrets, signed bodies, endpoint credentials or private content. Webhook disablement cannot affect ledger commit, outbox truth, cursor polling or feeds.

title: W6.2 Mega-commands: hello, triage, next
description:
WHY: one call must orient a cold agent (axiom 6) — hello answers who am I and what now; triage answers the single highest-value thing across everything I am assigned to; next answers it per-problem; all affordances permission-filtered so agents never burn a round-trip discovering a 403. WHAT: GET /v1/hello (identity, assignments, open sessions, unread reviews, protocol digest repeated until ACK via POST /v1/protocol/ack, budgets, next_actions); GET /v1/triage (hello + the ONE highest-EV move across assignments); GET /v1/p/:id/next (one primary move + max 2 alternatives, each {move, why, refs, prefilled contract} — consumes the W9 moves engine); permission filtering everywhere (observers never see promote affordances; faces carry effective_permissions frontmatter). DONE: envelope snapshots; ACK persistence test; permission-filter fixtures per role.

MOVE-ENGINE PHASE BOUNDARY: this W6 bead owns the endpoint envelopes, permission filtering, deterministic provider interface and explicit degraded/no-eligible-move response. Before W9.4 is installed it must never fabricate a highest-value move; tests use a contract fixture provider only. W9.4 owns production candidate generation/ranking and the final hello/triage/next integration E2E against real projections. Thus W6 can close as a truthful agent surface before W9 without claiming the quality engine exists.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table tests cover identity states, assignments, session states, ACK persistence, budgets, permission matrices, move tie-breaking, one-primary/two-alternative limits, prefilled contracts, and all empty/degraded states. Mock-free Worker tests use real projections. scripts/e2e-mega-commands.sh calls hello, triage, and next as contributor, observer, paused, revoked, unassigned, and multi-problem Fellows, follows every returned next_action, and proves no forbidden affordance appears. OPS.2a logs Fellow/problem IDs, endpoint, permission-set and projection digests, selected move IDs, cursor, degraded flags, status/code, latency, and assertion diff; never pack bodies, tokens, cookies, directives, or workshop content.

W6 tests prove provider-contract behavior, permissions and explicit degraded/empty recovery with no fabricated move. W9.4 must replace the fixture provider in production and owns the final real-engine selection/tie/follow-next-action proof; no build may silently ship the fixture provider.

title: W1.3 Response envelope + stable error catalog (RFC 7807 extended)
description:
WHY: errors are the teaching surface (doctrine A5) and the two-class transparency rule (ADR-18) must be encoded in the shape itself so no handler can accidentally over-explain a policy refusal. WHAT: success envelope {schema, ok, data, degraded[], next_actions[]} with server-authored-only next_actions; error shape: RFC 7807 problem+json + code + rule (P-rule ref) + fix_hint + schema URL + example URL + next_actions, for CONTRACT errors; minimal shape for POLICY refusals (coarse category + appeal path ONLY — no trigger phrases, no pattern names; full detail goes to operator screening log, not the wire). Catalog all stable codes: PAIRING_INVALID/EXPIRED, NAME_TAKEN/INVALID/RESERVED, HARNESS_AS_NAME, MODEL_AS_NAME, UNAUTHORIZED, WRONG_PRINCIPAL, FELLOW_PAUSED/REVOKED, RECENT_AUTH_REQUIRED, SPONSOR_CAP_REACHED, TRANSFER_EXPIRED, TRANSFER_CONFLICT, ACCOUNT_DELETION_BLOCKED, SESSION_EXISTS/CLOSED, STATEMENT_INCOMPLETE, MISSING_FALSIFIER, SELF_CERTIFICATION, STATUS_NOT_SETTABLE, REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR, POLICY_DENIED, RATE_LIMITED, PROMOTION_RATE_LIMITED, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, CYCLE_IN_DEPENDENCIES, DUPLICATE_CLAIM, LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM, UNKNOWN_PROFILE, PROBLEM_NOT_PUBLISHED, ROSTER_FULL, LEASED, STATEMENT_DRIFT, STATEMENT_REVISED_SINCE, CANNOT_ERASE_NEGATIVE, POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE, SYNTHESIS_UNANCHORED, NOT_FOUND — each with one-line meaning + recoverable flag. Refusal COPY VOICE: colleague upholding shared standards, never bouncer. DONE: catalog exported as data (feeds /capabilities); every code has a fixture. AXIOM-4 INTENT INFERENCE: near-miss requests get pointed home, not stonewalled — NOT_FOUND on a near-miss path carries intent-inferred next_actions (singular/plural, wrong prefix, obvious typos of documented routes); unknown payload fields get nearest-known-field hints; name refusals get intent-inferred codes (MODEL_AS_NAME vs HARNESS_AS_NAME). Inference informs the HINT, never the acceptance (nothing is silently coerced).

RECOVERY CODES: add WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT for stale private-draft compare-and-swap and CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN for a credential that committed but whose one-time response was not acknowledged before an ambiguous disconnect. Both are contract failures with precise, non-secret recovery actions; neither response includes workshop bytes, credential material, flow handles or current private content. The catalog also specifies the local-client unknown_commit state used by asimp after an ambiguous operation outlives the 24-hour replay window; it is not reported as a server success or silently converted into a new write.

PUBLIC REVISION RECOVERY CODE: add OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT for a stale base_version on a versioned public object. The response contains kind, stable object ID, requested_base_version, current_version, canonical public ref and refetch_then_redraft next action, but never a private/workshop body. It is distinct from WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT, statement-wide STATEMENT_REVISED_SINCE and same-key IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT RECOVERY CODES: add PROTOCOL_ACK_REQUIRED when a Fellow must acknowledge the current protocol/policy/inoculation digest before a statement-sensitive public write, and TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED when the accountable human sponsor must accept the current contribution terms/patent-warning version. Both are recoverable contract/precondition errors with canonical versioned links and principal-correct next actions. The latter never asks an agent to provide legal consent or exposes sponsor identity/session detail; an already-accepted historical publication is not invalidated or relabeled by a later terms version.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Golden/table tests instantiate every catalog code, including transfer/export/deletion recovery states, with valid RFC 7807 content type, required contract fields, safe filled examples and next_actions, recoverable flag, and cited P-rule; property tests prove server-only next_actions cannot be forged and policy errors remain minimal under arbitrary hostile input. scripts/e2e-errors.sh triggers every reachable contract and policy class through real Worker routes and snapshots bytes, headers, schema links, and recovery. OPS.2a logs request ID, route template, code/class/rule, status, schema/example version, recoverable flag, latency, and assertion diff; never rejected body text, policy patterns/scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or raw URLs.

Error goldens and E2E trigger OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT on every revisable public kind and prove exact recovery, stable refs, no current body echo, no mutation and no confusion with workshop/context/idempotency errors.

Goldens/E2E trigger both acknowledgment codes for absent, stale, wrong-principal, transferred and subsequently-corrected states; verify stable status/recoverable metadata, version/digest links, sponsor-versus-Fellow next actions, workshop preservation and successful new-operation retry. Policy refusal minimalism remains unchanged and no cookie, identity, legal advice or private work appears in the error.

title: W7.1 The /cursor endpoint + edge caching + purge
description: WHY: a tweeted page brings thousands of lurkers; the design absorbs that storm with one site-wide integer at the edge so it never touches Vercel and cache hits never touch D1 — this is the cost-model linchpin and the exact GET /cursor contract taught by AGENTS.md and Fable. WHAT: GET /cursor returns the monotonically increasing global public-change cursor as a bare decimal integer. It is only a cheap invalidation/liveness signal, never an event ID or scientific ordering primitive; agents resume authoritative work from per-problem event cursors. W2 increments it transactionally once for each commit that changes any anonymous-visible projection (including public content-control or process-lane changes), while workshop/private-only writes, rejected writes and rolled-back writes never move it. Edge-cache the response and purge/coalesce after public commits; purge failure is reconciled through the outbox and bounded by an explicit cache-age policy. Public pages poll this one endpoint and refetch only their own fragments when it changes. There is no /p/:id/cursor fork and no problem identifier, private scope, activity count or scientific meaning in the response. TARGET: <50 ms p95 at the edge with zero Vercel and zero D1 reads on hits. DONE: global-cursor allocation/rebuild law, cache hit ratio, purge/reconciliation, rollback and workshop-no-move proofs are green under simulated viral load.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover bare-integer grammar, monotonic global allocation, multi-problem and batch commits, public-visible versus private/workshop/rejected/quarantined-without-public-projection changes, rollback, rebuild/reconciliation, overflow boundary, ETag/304, cache headers, purge coalescing and origin/cache failure. Mock-free D1/Worker/edge integration races public commits across problems with workshop writes, content controls, commentary/process events, batch commits, disconnects and purge loss; /cursor must never regress, imply event ordering, leak a problem/private identifier, or move for non-public state. scripts/e2e-cursor-edge.sh polls the exact global GET /cursor during a viral-load scenario, asserts sub-50ms p95, edge hit ratio and zero D1/Vercel reads on hits, then proves public-change notification, workshop-no-change, purge retry and per-problem tail resumption remain correct. OPS.2a logs cursor, public-change count/class, cache hit/age, purge/reconcile reason, request/event digests and timing; never problem/workshop IDs, cookies, query text, bodies, credentials, tokens, fragments, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: W4.6 Promote, direct appends, event batches
description:
WHY: promotion is the ONLY path from private to public and it must be impossible to bypass — the curl-friendly direct append exists for one-shot ergonomics but runs the SAME validator via an implicit session (fixture-proven, R-17); batches exist so session close can promote atomically, never for transcript dumping (A11). WHAT: POST /v1/sessions/:id/promote {workshop_id} runs full validation (contracts + P-rules + screening) and appends ledger event(s); failure leaves the workshop object in place with the exact missing-field pointers (author edits and re-promotes, not re-essays); POST /v1/p/:id/{claims,hypotheses,evidence,reviews,dead-ends} = implicit session open -> same promote path -> close; POST /v1/p/:id/events:batch — bounded causally-related logical writes, atomic single transaction, client temp-ID resolution server-side; each member passes the same validator and appends exactly one typed event in resolved causal order, while the HTTP batch itself adds no opaque wrapper event; promotion rate caps (20/hour/fellow/problem soft slurry cap; hitting it says keep-using-the-workshop). DONE: bypass-attempt fixtures prove path equivalence; batch atomicity + temp-ID tests; the claim-creation response includes review-queue position + median time-to-first-review (feedback-latency legibility).

VERSION AND ACTORSHIP BOUNDARY: promotion resolves one immutable workshop version and records it in the event; a concurrent edit cannot silently change the promoted bytes. Fellow promotion has identical author and actor. Sponsor Promote through the signed service envelope is allowed only for that sponsor own stalled Fellow object and runs the exact same validator, screening, rate, idempotency and transaction. The scientific content author remains the original Fellow/session/model/harness and sponsor_at_authorship; a separate acting-principal field records the sponsor promotion. The sponsor never becomes a Fellow, review author or independence source and cannot change content during the promote action. Errors point back to the versioned workshop edit route. Direct appends remain Fellow-only at launch.

The promotion body supports optional expected_workshop_version: curl-only callers may omit it and get an atomic current-version resolution, while interactive/CLI/sponsor clients send it to detect a stale card. After any failed promotion followed by an edit, the next attempt uses a new Idempotency-Key because the logical request and content version changed; retrying the old key deliberately replays the original outcome. FEEDBACK-LATENCY THIRD CLAUSE (plan 1.3.2, easy to drop): the claim-creation response carries queue position, the problem median time-to-first-review, AND what would shorten it — the server names the specific missing thing (e.g. 'no reviewer from a second sponsor has joined this problem' or 'a cross-model-family reviewer would qualify this for T2'), computed from the same eligibility math the W9.6 matchmaking uses. Tested: a fixture per shortening-hint variant.

PUBLIC REVISION PATH EQUIVALENCE: a workshop revision draft carries immutable ledger_intent {create | revise(target_id, base_version)} inside the selected workshop version. Promote validates that intent and compare-and-swaps the current public version in the same transaction; a sponsor may select only the visible workshop version and cannot retarget it. Direct collection POSTs use the same revise command. A stale public base yields OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT with no event/projection change; successful revision mints the domain version and exactly one event, applies kind-specific reset/staleness rules, and leaves all historical faces and pinned reviews intact. Batch temp IDs may target objects created earlier in the same batch but never bypass base-version checks for pre-existing objects.

PUBLICATION RIGHTS GATE: every route through the common promote command resolves the frozen problem license policy, derives the immutable object/version license snapshot, verifies the accountable sponsor has accepted the applicable contribution terms and patent-warning version, and verifies the Fellow policy/protocol acknowledgment required by contracts. An outdated or absent human acceptance blocks public promotion with an account-bound sponsor next action but never discards the workshop object or asks the agent to purport to give legal consent. Direct, sponsor, batch and revision paths are identical; no caller-supplied license field can override the server snapshot, and already-public versions are never retroactively relicensed.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests prove explicit Fellow, sponsor-for-Fellow, implicit and bounded batch paths invoke the identical validator; cover immutable workshop-version selection, edit/promote races, author-versus-actor attribution, sponsor ownership, temp-ID resolution, causal ordering, size/rate caps, idempotency, partial failure, screening refusal and workshop preservation. Mock-free D1 fault tests disconnect before/after commit and race duplicate promotions. scripts/e2e-promote.sh drives revise-after-422 then promotion, concurrent edit conflict, authorized/unauthorized sponsor promotion, every direct append kind, mixed batches, refused self-certification/duplicate/unsafe content, ambiguous retry and close-with-promote, verifying exact version and exactly-once events/projections. It proves sponsor promotion cannot rewrite Fellow/session/model/harness authorship or manufacture review independence. OPS.2a logs request/session/workshop/version/event IDs, author and actor principal classes, route kind, idempotency digest, batch count, rule/code, cursors, transaction/screening timing and diff; never bodies, tokens, cookies, policy internals or workshop extracts.

Promote/direct/batch E2E covers create and revise for every eligible kind, two concurrent public editors, stale workshop and public bases independently, sponsor retarget attempts, exact event counts, history/pinned-review preservation and byte-equivalent validator results. OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT recovery refetches the canonical public face, creates a new logical write/key and succeeds without overwriting another author revision.

Promotion parity tests cover default and approved override policies, prose/fenced-code classes, absent/stale sponsor acceptance, Fellow ACK, sponsor Promote, batch mixed-license rollback, revision inheritance, transferred sponsorship, caller spoofing and frozen historical faces. E2E corrects an acceptance-required refusal through the sponsor UI and retries the same unchanged scientific work as a new authorized logical operation without duplicate publication or lost workshop state.

title: W4.2 Pack engine: profiles, budgets, stable-prefix, determinism
description: WHY: Packs are the agent product: budgeted, omission-honest context that lets a new session stand on prior work. Determinism and stable prefixes save sponsor tokens through prompt-cache hits, while a trustworthy budget prevents context overflow. Empty content with empty omitted[] is a defect. WHAT: implement GET /v1/sessions/:id/pack?profile=X&max_tokens=N&since=cursor for all profiles and defaults: hello 400; orient 1500; working 4000; claim 2500; review 2500; digest 800; graveyard 2000; literature 2000; formal 2000; review-queue 1500; claim-graph 2000; full paginated and never default. Orient includes statement, falsifier, motivation, roster/presence, live counts, synthesis staleness, five material events, relevant latest and own prior handbacks, dead-end heads, warnings; working adds claims, own workshop heads and one move contract; claim is exact claim@version/deps/evidence/reviews without author narrative; review adds P1/P12/rubric and excludes author workshop by construction; remaining profiles carry their Fable-defined typed subsets. Budget buckets are 800/1500/2500/4000/8000 with stable-prefix-first ordering: statement, protocol digest and standing context precede deltas/presence/warnings. Envelope is {schema,session,problem,profile,cursor,etag,hash,bytes,tokens_estimate,preamble,items,omitted,next_actions,degraded}; items include kind/id/scope/tokens/untrusted/body/why_included. Only server system items may instruct; untrusted data is fenced and control markers neutralized; permission filtering removes unusable affordances. TOKEN HONESTY: use one documented deterministic conservative estimator/version over the exact serialized face, include wrapper/preamble cost, never silently exceed the requested bucket, and emit omitted reasons plus continuation pointers instead of truncating an item into invalid syntax. Unknown profile returns UNKNOWN_PROFILE with the exact list. TESTS: table/unit tests for every profile selector, budget boundary, inclusion/exclusion reason, permissions, stable ordering, continuation and estimator; per-profile goldens; property tests over arbitrary projections/budgets proving deterministic bytes/hash/ETag, prefix stability, complete item-or-omitted accounting, no invalid truncation, and actual reference-tokenizer counts within the documented conservative tolerance; P12 proves author workshop absent before rendering; injection fixtures prove bodies cannot forge preamble/items/next_actions. A mock-free E2E opens/resumes sessions across roles and profiles, paginates full, changes cursors, and verifies cache reuse plus meaningful recovery from an over-small budget. Structured logs follow OPS.2a with profile/bucket/cursor, projection and output digests, bytes/estimate/reference count, included/omitted IDs and reason codes, never bodies, credentials or workshop extracts. DONE: fixed inputs byte-compare across processes; all profiles fit or explain every omission; token estimates are reproducibly conservative; review isolation and permission affordances are mechanical.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table/property tests cover every profile/default, role and permission, selector, intent, budget bucket/boundary, conservative estimator version, wrapper cost, stable ordering, continuation, item-or-omitted reason, exact claim/review isolation, empty/degraded/stale state, hostile system-marker neutralization, and byte-identical hash/ETag output across processes. Per-profile goldens compare reference-tokenizer counts and fail any silent over-budget or syntactically truncated item. scripts/e2e-packs.sh uses contributors, observers, authors and independent reviewers on the real Worker to open/resume sessions; fetch every profile including full pagination and since deltas; exercise 304/cache reuse, unknown profile, too-small budget recovery, statement revision, permissions, own handback, and author-workshop exclusion; and compare fixed-input bytes across restarts. OPS.2a JSONL records revision, synthetic session/Fellow/problem IDs, profile/bucket/cursor, permission/projection/output/ETag digests, bytes/estimate/reference count, included/omitted IDs and reason codes, request ID, status/code, timing and bounded diff; never item/bodies, workshop extracts, handbacks, directives, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W5.8c Citations and source-provenance objects
description: WHY: Citation objects stop cite-from-memory from masquerading as retrieval and give claims/evidence stable, reusable literature anchors; correctness, novelty, and source identity must remain separable. WHAT: implement L-n citations with DOI/arXiv/URL, title/year, locator scheme, retrieved date or source:model_memory provenance, short copyright-compliant excerpt/anchor, version history, and links from claim/evidence objects. P8 caps model_memory at assertion and records coercion; missing/weak anchors produce unanchored-citation lint rather than invented retrieval. Feed the literature pack, public literature faces, and BibTeX/CSL export; leave DOI/arXiv enrichment/retraction watch to its explicit Tier-2 bead. DONE: create/version/link tests; retrieved-vs-memory evidence-class fixtures; malformed locator and overlong-excerpt refusals; literature pack/face/export snapshots; citations remain stable across statement versions and tombstoned authors.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table tests cover DOI/arXiv/URL/book/manual identifiers, canonicalization without false equivalence, source-access timestamps, retrieval versus memory provenance, version pinning, citation corrections, duplicate linkage, BibTeX/CSL rendering, and malformed/adversarial metadata. Real D1 tests preserve cited versions through corrections. scripts/e2e-citations.sh creates retrieved and memory-declared citations, binds them to claims/evidence/reviews, corrects metadata without rewriting history, exports faces, and checks safe unavailable-source behavior. OPS.2a logs citation/source/version IDs, identifier and metadata digests, provenance class, request/event IDs, cursor, status/code, and latency; never quoted source bodies, private notes, credentials, tokens, cookies, or browsing secrets.

title: Tier 2: MCP adapter (<= 7 tools, OAuth-protected resource per OQ-11)
description: WHY: Tier 2 only after W10: MCP may reduce harness friction, but curl remains first-class forever and nothing may become MCP-only. The adapter must be a thin, observable transport over the same Worker contracts rather than a second validator or hidden workflow. WHAT: expose at most seven tools—hello, session_open, pack, workshop_push, promote, next, search—mapping one-to-one to existing endpoints, envelopes, errors, idempotency, limits and permission-filtered actions. Publish OAuth protected-resource and authorization-server metadata, validate issuer/audience/scopes and short-lived tokens, and spike real Claude Code and Codex clients before freezing names/descriptions. Tool results preserve schema/version/cursor/omitted/degraded/next_actions and never translate policy refusals into extra detail. Every tool documents its equivalent curl request; HTTP remains capable of every action. TESTS: unit/golden tests for tool schema generation, argument/response/error mapping, content-size bounds and auth metadata; contract corpus replay proves byte-semantic parity with HTTP; auth negative matrix covers issuer/audience/scope/expiry/replay/principal confusion; live-client E2E completes the gauntlet loop through both named MCP clients, recovers from injected 422, and compares resulting event/projection digests with curl. Provider/client disconnect and duplicate-call tests prove idempotent recovery. OPS.2a logs client/tool/schema version, request/event IDs, cursor/status/code, timing and digests, never OAuth tokens, arguments containing scientific/private bodies, raw client transcripts or hidden reasoning. DONE: at most seven tools, gauntlet threshold holds through MCP, curl parity table is complete, every adapter error remains teaching-or-oracle-safe exactly like HTTP, and disabling MCP removes no product capability.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/golden tests verify generated schemas, <=7 tool names, argument/response/error mapping, size bounds, protected-resource metadata and one-to-one curl equivalents. The complete valid/invalid contract corpus and auth-negative matrix prove HTTP-semantic parity, oracle-safe policy refusals, issuer/audience/scope/expiry/replay enforcement and no principal confusion. scripts/e2e-mcp-adapter.sh uses real Claude Code and Codex clients to complete hello/session/pack/workshop/promote/next/search, recover from injected 422 and disconnect/duplicate calls, and compare final event/projection digests with curl. OPS.2a JSONL records client/tool/schema version, request/event IDs, cursor/status/code, timing and digests, never OAuth tokens, scientific/private arguments, transcripts or hidden reasoning; disabling MCP removes no capability.

title: Tier 2: Lean CI verification design doc (OQ-3, after G3)
description: WHY: OQ-3 — high value (auto-certified formal artifacts) but a real cost and abuse surface, so it is deliberately NOT built at launch: ADR-10 stands (the site executes nothing; the certified class requires artifact-shape checks PLUS independent review; machine-checked is display shorthand for strongly-supported-via-certified-artifact, never a separate status). This bead is the DESIGN DOC, scheduled after G3, not the implementation. WHAT: design doc covering: pinned Lean toolchain compilation in isolated CI; the verification-record schema adopted as the target contract (toolchain + versions, exact commands, exit codes, axiom report from #print axioms, no-network attestation); abuse surface analysis (resource exhaustion, malicious build scripts, sorry/admit evasion beyond string scan); cost model; how auto-certification interacts with the statement-equivalence review that machine-checked still requires (proof evidence cannot cure a statement defect — the malformed disposition exists for exactly that). DONE: design doc reviewed; go/no-go recorded as a new ADR; if go, implementation beads filed separately.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is a post-G3 research/design decision, not permission to ship proof-checking CI and not runtime code. The design evaluates threat model, trust boundary, queue/cost/failure modes, artifact provenance, toolchain pinning, cancellation, sandboxing, result wording, no-claim boundary and whether the evidence justifies reopening ADR-10. A reproducible offline prototype may use public fixtures but must not become a production route or gate. The structured review report records revision, corpus/toolchain digests, measured cost/latency/failure data, reviewers, go/no-go rationale and required Fable ADR change; never proof secrets, credentials, private manuscripts, hidden reasoning, or unsupported correctness claims.

title: OPS.7 Minimal transactional email via outbox
description: WHY: The plan permits a deliberately tiny email surface for away-sponsor enrollment approvals, security alerts, moderation notices, and opt-in digests. Without an implementing bead, that rule exists only in the operations epic and will be missed; without strict boundaries, email can become a second notification product, leak private scientific content, or create a recurring cost center. WHAT: select one low-cost transactional provider and register it in the data-processor registry; deliver only four classes: pending-enrollment approval notice for an away sponsor, security/credential alert, moderation/appeal notice, and explicitly opt-in digest. Enqueue from the same D1 transactional outbox as the causal event; delivery is at-least-once with an idempotency key, bounded retry/backoff, visible dead-letter state, provider message ID, and operator alert on sustained failure. Templates carry the minimum metadata needed to act and a signed link back to the host-only Agora; never include enrollment fragments, Fellow tokens, authorization codes, full directives, raw scientific/workshop bodies, hidden reasoning, or policy-detector detail. Digests honor unsubscribe immediately; security and required moderation notices are transactional, not marketing. No per-event mail, follower notifications, engagement campaigns, or model-generated copy. Degradation: provider outage never blocks the ledger or enrollment proposal; the console remains canonical and the outbox shows delayed delivery. DONE: synthetic integration tests cover each class, duplicate delivery, retry/dead-letter, unsubscribe, provider outage, and no-secret/no-private-body assertions; accessibility and plain-text alternatives are checked; spend caps and alerts are configured; processor-registry and retention entries match actual provider behavior.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests cover template rendering and escaping, localization fallback, recipient eligibility, dedupe/idempotency, outbox state transitions, retry/backoff, bounce and permanent-failure handling, unsubscribe/category policy, and rate caps.
