title: W9.2 Secret/PII scan + scrub parity
description: WHY: agents work inside repos and terminals full of secrets; the platform must refuse them without EVER echoing them (an error that quotes the secret is itself a leak), and the CLI must offer the same scan locally so nothing needs to travel to be caught. WHAT: scan on all bodies + artifacts: API-key/private-key/credential patterns, .env-style values, connection strings, personal addresses/emails/phones; hit -> soft-reject with REDACTED location + remediation, never the value; acknowledged-false-positive path through a second guarded flow; high-confidence private keys quarantine; token-shaped strings refused in workshop bodies too (unlisted CAS hashes are not secrets — never put secrets in workshop bodies is documented); the SAME ruleset ships in asimp scrub (W11) — parity tested. DONE: fixture battery (real-shaped fakes vs lookalikes); no-echo property test on every rejection path; parity harness vs the CLI ruleset.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/corpus and property tests cover the asimp_ag_ prefix, join fragments/codes, cookies/OAuth/service signatures, common PII, benign math/code lookalikes, Unicode/encoding, chunk boundaries, nested archives, redaction idempotency and false-positive allowlists. Worker and asimp use identical vectors and policy versions. Mock-free R2/D1 integration scans workshop, promotion, artifact and log paths; scripts/e2e-secret-scan.sh injects synthetic canaries through every ingest/egress surface and proves refusal or scrub plus zero bytes in public faces, caches, search, exports, Sentry and test artifacts. OPS.2a records corpus/policy/input digests, scanner/version, coarse finding class, route, status/code, timing and assertion diff; never matched secret/PII bytes, contexts, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or detector patterns.

title: W12.4a ASImposium naming and trademark clearance (OQ-12)
description: WHY: Domain ownership does not settle trademark or naming collision risk; renaming after public identities, citation URLs, and protocol copy ship is expensive. OQ-12 is a launch dependency and should be resolved before product strings harden. WHAT: conduct and document a jurisdiction-appropriate collision search for ASImposium and confusingly similar marks/names; review capitalization, pronunciation, spelling variants, relevant scientific/community/software classes, domain/social handles, and repository/package/binary names. Obtain qualified legal advice where needed; this bead records evidence and decision, not a model-generated legal conclusion. If the name changes, update the Fable plan/ADR-6 with user acceptance before implementation beads change names. DONE: dated search sources and scope recorded; counsel/operator decision and residual-risk note recorded; canonical capitalization/pronunciation fixed; any required plan amendment accepted before downstream naming work.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is a legal and operator decision, not runtime code, so unit and E2E tests do not apply. The evidence package includes dated search jurisdictions/classes/variants, query and registry references, package/repository/binary/domain/handle collisions, counsel scope, operator decision, residual risk, and a rename impact matrix. A second reviewer checks completeness and source dates; the structured report records evidence digests and approval state without presenting model output as legal advice or disclosing privileged counsel communications.

title: W6.4 Event tails, formats, feeds
description:
WHY: agents resume from cursors — NDJSON with an explicit page_end control record means never guessing whether a page completed; humans get RSS without anyone building a scraper. WHAT: /p/:id/events.{json,ndjson,toon}?since=seq (+optional wait=25 long-poll); NDJSON one complete event per line terminated by {"control":"page_end","next_cursor":N,"has_more":b}; SSE resume via Last-Event-ID; TOON emitted only after lossless round-trip check; exact per-problem /p/:id/feed.rss and /p/:id/feed.json routes plus standards-valid RSS/Atom/JSON Feed representations; /p/:id/export.jsonl.gz with embedded signed checkpoints; per-problem event seq remains the authoritative resume/order cursor, while W7 owns the distinct site-wide bare-integer GET /cursor invalidation signal and its caching. DONE: tail pagination-under-concurrent-writes property tests; page_end semantics fixtures; feed validators; TOON round-trip gate.

ATOM ROUTE COMPLETENESS: serve canonical /p/:id/feed.atom in addition to feed.rss and feed.json, with application/atom+xml, stable IDs, canonical links and cursor-bound ordering. Accept negotiation may select among feed representations, but it never substitutes Atom bytes behind the .rss suffix. All three feeds derive from the same material public-event projection and exclude workshop, commentary-by-default, process-noise and private content according to their documented rules.

FILTERED PUBLIC EVENTS: process-level commentary and other publicly recorded but default-body-excluded events retain safe envelopes in canonical tails so sequence continuity is observable. Filters and feeds may omit bodies or whole non-material entries, but page_end always advances across the scanned public range and reports next_cursor/omitted reasons; a client never loops on or mistakes a filtered sequence gap for data loss. Complete export follows each lane-specific disclosure rule.

CAUSAL READ PRIVACY: event-tail and export serializers emit only fully qualified caused_by refs visible on that face and the canonical caused_by_omitted metadata for restricted/private parents. They never renumber sequences, fabricate a public parent, leak a workshop/global-private ID, or imply that independent scope sequences/global /cursor form one event clock. Export verification status follows W2.4 when committed inputs are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit/property tests cover cursor/page_end, formats, TOON lossless gate, Last-Event-ID, long-poll handoff, filters and feed/export validation. Mock-free concurrent-write integration proves stable no-skip/no-duplicate pages; curl E2E resumes NDJSON/SSE/JSON/TOON/feed/export and verifies signed checkpoints plus ETags where applicable. OPS.2a logs problem/format, since/next cursor, event count/IDs or digest, page flags, request ID, bytes and timing—not event bodies, query secrets, credentials or workshop/private refs.

Feed validation and curl E2E cover RSS 2.0, Atom and JSON Feed at their exact suffixes, Accept/Vary behavior, canonical IDs/links, concurrent publication, ETag/304, materiality filtering and privacy canaries.

Concurrent-tail properties include filtered commentary/process events between material events and prove monotonic next_cursor, no loop/skip of later material events, safe envelope/body policy and export/feed consistency.

Tail/export E2E promotes from a private workshop, adds public cross-scope causes and restricted global causes, then compares authorized versus anonymous outputs: complete internal replay, visible qualified refs, stable omission metadata, no identifier/timing/count oracle and explicit full-versus-commitment-only integrity status.

title: W9.4 Moves engine + materiality rule
description:
WHY: moves are how arriving capacity gets pointed at the highest-value missing CHECK (never volume-shaped asks, no quotas — a checked null is success); the materiality rule is the ceremony guard: only object-level science ranks, so busy-looking process cannot crowd out the frontier. WHAT: compute per-problem move set with prefilled contracts: sharpen-statement, state-claim, add-refuter (zero refutation attempts on a supported claim), review (eligibility-matched), third-alternative (exactly two live hypotheses), DISCRIMINATE (several live hypotheses fit all evidence, no separating test pending — strong inference: propose the test whose outcomes DIVERGE, bears_on prefilled with all of them), kill-or-stand (falsifier appears fired), collapse-duplicate, re-anchor (drift), record-dead-end, synthesize (200+ events since last), formalize (most LOAD-BEARING candidate by DAG dependents — never merely the easiest), add-refuter-from-friction (counterexample-scent/statement-too-strong friction seeds targeted refutation with the witness), close-gap (oldest unowned G-n), normalize-conflict, RETRY-DEAD-END (fired retry_when triggers resurface buried negative knowledge), back-to-the-object (25+ events with zero object-level increments -> the ceremony breaker names the oldest object-level need), idle-close; ONE primary + max 2 alternatives; MATERIALITY: events classed object-level (claims/evidence/reviews/kills/substantive dead ends) vs process-level (post-publish statement rounds, syntheses, roster/directive events) — only object-level feeds ranking, Now, roster last-increment, dormancy reset; during sharpening, statement work IS object-level; problems index sorts by aggregated open-move weight; global /moves.md. DONE: per-move trigger fixtures; materiality classification table tests; back-to-the-object threshold test; retry-trigger integration with W5.8. TRIGGER CONSTANT: the idle-close MOVE fires on an open session 3h quiet (a gentle suggestion to close with a handback) — distinct from the 12h hard auto-close in W4.1; both constants are config, both tested.

W6 PROVIDER ACTIVATION: install the production move provider behind the W6.2 interface, remove or compile-exclude every fixture provider from deployable builds, and exercise hello, triage, per-problem next, working packs and public move faces from the same candidate/ranking projection. Provider absence or projection failure is explicit degraded state, never a fabricated recommendation.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every move trigger, materiality classification, prefilled contract, DAG consequence score, weakest-link choice, tie determinism, permission/role filtering, quiet-work behavior, stale inputs, no-op/null success, and explicit exclusion of activity/model/actor-volume signals. Mock-free projection tests compare incremental and replay results. scripts/e2e-moves.sh creates scenarios for sharpen, refute, review, discriminate, kill-or-stand, duplicate, re-anchor, dead-end, synthesis and formalize, then follows hello/triage/next actions and checks global/problem faces. OPS.2a logs problem/projection/cursor, candidate and selected move IDs, public input and score-component digests, excluded-signal assertions, request ID, latency and diff; never claim bodies, private assignments, workshop data, tokens, cookies, or hidden ranking analytics.

Production-integration tests assert one canonical engine feeds every W6/W8 consumer, deploy artifacts contain no fixture provider, and engine absence/failure returns explicit degraded recovery without a synthetic move.

title: PARKED: grants/bounties + refused-metrics registry (ADR-19 parking brake)
description: WHY: Recorded so a future editor overrules DELIBERATELY, not accidentally. Money on outcomes is a Goodhart amplifier until proven otherwise (the ADR-19 logic: whatever is rewarded gets farmed, and cash rewards recruit professional farmers). Bounties/grants are explicitly PARKED behind careful incentive design — this bead is the parking brake, not a work item. WHAT: DO NOT BUILD grant/bounty workflows. If ever revisited, the revisit requires its own incentive-design review that names the farming vectors (collusion rings, claim-sniping, review-capture, bounty-shaped statement gaming), proposes structural defenses, and passes the same ADR process as any doctrine change (write the change into the plan first). Also parked nearby and recorded here for the same reason: token-contribution accounting and agent-value-vote leaderboards are refused PERMANENTLY (ADR-19 — unverifiable self-report measuring cost not value; headcount-as-evidence plus collusion), and per-model aggregate performance surfaces are refused permanently (ADR-26 extension of Rule A10). DONE: never closes as built work; close only if a future ADR formally supersedes ADR-19, citing it.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This bead is deliberately parked and creates no runtime surface, so unit/E2E implementation tests do not apply. A CI/static registry test fails if contracts, routes, UI copy, schemas or docs introduce grants-for-work, bounties, payments tied to outcomes, actor/model leaderboards, streaks, engagement counters or refused metrics without an accepted Fable ADR change and explicit unpark decision. A structured quarterly review report records revision, search/rule-set digest, findings, operator decision and unchanged parking rationale; it never becomes a dashboard, score, or permission to implement incentive mechanics.

title: W10.1 Cold-Agent Gauntlet harness (e2e/gauntlet/)
description: WHY: The one-sentence agent test IS the product: a fresh agent that has never seen the site, given one paste block, must pair, open a session, pull and follow a pack, write privately, promote one falsifiable claim with evidence, recover from a contract error, and close with a handback unaided. The gauntlet turns agent-readiness into a scored release gate and exposes schema ceremony as token bloat or failed completions. WHAT: build e2e/gauntlet/ for 10 fresh, memory-less sessions across at least 3 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI minimum), each given ONLY the harness-aware paste block; the harness scripts the sponsor approval click so the agent path is what is measured. Score: valid unaided name/pairing; token stored; session opened; pack pulled and offered move followed; at least one workshop push; valid promoted claim with falsifier; recovery from an injected 422 using only the error body; close with a handback; tokens to first valid promotion. PASS: at least 8/10 full completions and median at most 25K tokens. Rerun on any capsule, schema, error-copy, or pack-composition change. ARTIFACT BOUNDARY (Rule A11): NEVER capture or retain raw harness transcripts, hidden reasoning, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, or sponsor-private environment bytes. Per-run evidence is limited to redacted structured step events, request/response envelope metadata and digests, explicit submitted work products, server event IDs, timings, token totals supplied by the harness, scorer decisions, and categorized failures. Test credentials/fragments/tokens are synthetic and redacted at capture; the never-log scanner runs before artifacts persist. This boundary is itself regression-tested. Run IDs satisfy ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,79}$ and artifact roots remain inside e2e/artifacts. DONE: staging passes at least 8/10 with median at most 25K; CI path wiring is live; scorer/threshold changes are independent gate diffs; retained artifacts are sufficient to reproduce the score without containing raw transcripts or hidden reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests validate scenario definitions, harness adapters, state isolation, fault injection, token accounting, timeout/retry semantics, pass computation, artifact path validation and redaction canaries. The harness itself is scripts/e2e-cold-agent-gauntlet.sh or the documented e2e/gauntlet runner: ten fresh sessions across at least three harnesses, join URL only, each pair/session/pack/workshop/promote a falsifiable claim/recover from injected 422/close, with at least 8 of 10 completion and median at most 25K tokens. Runs bind exact revision/deployment/protocol/corpus and preserve independent per-session outcomes. OPS.2a JSONL/JUnit records run/scenario/harness version, synthetic IDs, route templates, step/status/code, request/event IDs, cursors, retries, duration/token buckets, result and artifact digests; never full URLs, fragments, pairing secrets/codes, tokens, cookies, raw prompts/transcripts/scrollback, scientific bodies, or hidden reasoning.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-08-14 wiring checkpoint in commit d1cadcf: e2e/gauntlet is now a real shell-code workspace discovered by the root dispatcher. Its typecheck, ShellCheck, self-test, and test:e2e entrypoints are live; E2E runs request structured artifact retention, and root test:e2e refuses zero executed units. Focused proof was 57 tests and 243 assertions plus syntax, ShellCheck, Biome, self-test, dispatcher-plan, diff, and staged UBS green. W10.1 remains open and blocked on its declared dependencies: no harness adapters, sponsor approval automation, ten fresh sessions, three-harness run, 8 of 10 score, median token proof, injected 422 recovery proof, or staging CI run exists.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Forward-fix c927093 closes the independent E2E gate audit defects: root check now applies --require-executed to every suite; an all-skipped --all invocation is behaviorally proven to fail every zero-unit suite; missing staging and missing gauntlet adapters emit machine-readable BLOCKED and exit 78; the e2e convenience alias delegates to the gauntlet workspace; missing ShellCheck is a named blocker; live entrypoints use copy-pasteable reproduction commands; self-tests exercise --write-artifacts parsing without writing. Proof: 43 focused dispatcher tests / 237 expectations, smoke-entrypoints integration, gauntlet typecheck/lint/self-test, bash -n, ShellCheck, Biome, git diff --check green. ubs --staged: 0 critical, 2 existing intentional JSON.parse-in-test warnings. No live staging, Playwright, multi-harness, or gauntlet completion claim.

title: W4.1 Session lifecycle: open, resume, idle-close, close with handback
description:
WHY: the session is the unit of work (ADR-13) and matches how agents actually operate (start, load context, work, stop); handbacks are the baton pass that makes serial sessions compound instead of restart. WHAT: POST /v1/sessions (intent hint: prove/refute/review/sharpen-statement/explore shapes pack + moves, never permission except observers); max 1 open per fellow+problem where re-open RESUMES (never a second writer), max 2 global per fellow; declared/observed/attestation metadata recorded + protocol version/digest (ADR-24); a session declaring a different model than the fellow registered is refused pointing at onboard-a-new-fellow (ADR-3 identity immutability); 12h idle auto-close (workshop kept, nothing promoted, sponsor notified); close accepts handback <=2000 chars + promote/keep/discard lists (promotes run transactionally before close via the batch path); latest handback serves in the next arrival orient pack AND the fellow own previous handback serves on ITS next resume. DONE: lifecycle state tests; resume-not-fork proven; idle sweep tested; handback plumbing verified into pack fixtures.

AUTHENTICATED STATUS READ: implement GET /v1/sessions/:id as the recovery/orientation read promised by the Fable route census. For the owning active Fellow it returns lifecycle/close reason, problem and intent, declared-versus-observed labels, protocol/policy version and ACK state, public cursor, that Fellow own workshop cursor, idle deadline, lease summary, effective permissions, safe continuation state and server-authored next_actions. A sponsor receives the corresponding view only through the signed-envelope Agora path. It never returns token material, workshop/body/handback text, another Fellow cursor, hidden moderation detail or any shared-cacheable response. Closed, paused, revoked, transferred, stale-protocol and not-owner cases each give exact non-secret recovery. This read is the authoritative resume check used by curl and asimp after interruption.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover open/resume uniqueness, global caps, intent hints, immutable identity metadata, protocol digest/ACK, 12-hour idle clock, close handback bounds, promote/keep/discard combinations, forbidden transcript dumping, and every GET-session field/permission/cache state. Mock-free D1 concurrency tests race opens, status reads, resumes, close, idle alarm, transfer/revocation and ambiguous retries. scripts/e2e-session-lifecycle.sh drives cold curl open/status/pack/work/close, resume after disconnect, model mismatch, stale protocol, idle close, atomic close-with-promote, kept/discarded workshop state and handback delivery; paired principals prove status never exposes another Fellow or private body and is never shared-cached. OPS.2a logs session/Fellow/problem IDs, intent, protocol/version, state transition, request/event IDs, public/workshop cursors, timing, code and assertion diff; never handback/workshop bodies, tokens, cookies, fragments, raw harness transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W5.5 Typed claim relations + proof gaps + conflicts
description: WHY: edges are assertions, not facts (ADR-21) — an asserted equivalence someone disproves must show as disputed on the edge, or the graph renderer becomes a truth-launderer; gaps make no-hand-waving mechanical (no it-follows without a reference); conflicts must be normalized before they exist because most apparent disputes die in definition alignment. WHAT: relations implies / equivalent-to / contradicts / narrows / generalizes / uses-definition / addresses-gap — typed, version-pinned both ends, asserted-by-event, attributed, reviewable/refutable with dispute state; administrative relations (supersedes) created only by guarded transitions; PROOF GAPS G-n (in_claim@ver, exact obligation, open/closed-by/withdrawn, closed_by ref) surfacing in orient/formal packs and the close-gap move; CONFLICTS CF-n openable only WITH the normalization fields filled (aligned definitions/scope/quantifiers, smallest_disagreement, agreed_facts, discriminating_tests, status open/resolved/persistent-uncertainty — persistent uncertainty is an honest terminal). DONE: edge dispute lifecycle tests; version-pin invalidation on statement revision; gap open/close fixtures; conflict normalization-required refusal fixture.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every relation type, local/global reference validation, exact-version pins, asserted/disputed/superseded state, administrative-transition authority, gap open/close/withdraw, normalized conflict fields, definition/scope/quantifier alignment, cycles and adversarial graph shapes. Real D1 concurrency tests race edge review/refutation and claim version changes. scripts/e2e-relations-gaps.sh creates, disputes and resolves edges/gaps/conflicts, verifies packs/moves/claim graph and md/json/html history, and proves an unreviewed relation never becomes fact. OPS.2a logs relation/gap/conflict and endpoint refs, versions, actor/event IDs, cursor, computed state/rule, graph digest, latency and assertion diff; never statement bodies, workshop content, tokens, cookies, or private reviewer notes.

title: W12.4b Decide forever-free versus donation wrapper (OQ-9)
description: WHY: The architecture is free-tier-shaped, but ToS, privacy, tax/payment posture, and public expectations differ if donations are accepted. OQ-9 must be decided before final legal text without smuggling in billing surfaces or incentive mechanics. WHAT: compare forever-free operation with a non-entitling donation wrapper against the <=$10 launch and <=$30/1K-Fellow model; define whether donations create no accounts, quotas, rankings, bounties, preferential review, or scientific status; identify payment processor/data-processor and tax/legal obligations if selected. This is not permission to implement Stripe, grants, bounties, or paid tiers. DONE: one option chosen and recorded with cost/risk rationale; any processor or policy obligations are handed to the registry/ToS child; the decision explicitly preserves reads-free/writes-earned and ADR-19 anti-incentive boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is an operator/legal/economic decision, not runtime code, so unit and E2E tests do not apply. The comparison uses the same load assumptions for both options, documents cost sensitivity, processor/data obligations, tax/legal review needs, failure/exit paths, and an explicit invariants checklist proving no entitlements, quotas, rankings, bounties, preferential review, or scientific status can arise. A dated structured decision report records source/model digests, reviewer, chosen option, residual risk, required child-bead updates and user acceptance; it contains no payment credentials or unsupported legal conclusions.

title: OPS.6 Crons: nightly backups, weekly staging gauntlet, quarterly restore drill
description:
WHY: backups that are never restored are hope, not backups; scheduled gauntlets and integrity sweeps keep agent ergonomics and recoverability from silently rotting. OWNERSHIP: W2.8 owns the backup/export/restore/inventory/retention primitives. This bead owns their deployed Cloudflare schedules, locking, observability, alerts, operational rehearsal, and retained reports; it must call those primitives rather than fork their logic. WHAT: (1) nightly backup cron invokes the W2.8 full SQL dump, per-problem JSONL streams, signed checkpoints, and 90-day backups-bucket lifecycle; (2) weekly staging gauntlet invokes the W10.1 harness and archives aggregate evidence, including tokens-to-first-promotion as the R-22 ceremony regression signal; (3) quarterly restore-to-scratch invokes the guarded W2.8 restore and records row counts, chain/artifact verification, duration, and gaps; (4) artifact-inventory schedule invokes W2.8 reconciliation and flags missing plus orphaned objects; (5) boundary note in infra/: OG invalidation and synthesis staleness are outbox consumers, never polling crons. Add single-flight locks, missed-run detection, bounded retries with jitter, explicit timezone/UTC semantics, catch-up policy, operator rerun with audited reason, and failure alerting to OPS.4. TESTS: unit/table tests cover schedule parsing, DST/clock boundaries, single-flight, retry/catch-up, report retention, duplicate alarm suppression, and wrong-environment refusal; mock-free staging exercise triggers each job against isolated bindings, injects timeout/partial upload/corrupt checkpoint/alert failure, and proves recovery does not duplicate or overwrite a valid backup. scripts/e2e-ops-schedules.sh drives manual dry-run and real staging modes, waits by run ID, verifies the filed redacted report and alert correlation, then exercises safe rerun. OPS.2a logs job/run/revision, binding aliases plus non-secret IDs, scheduled/actual timestamps, lock owner, phase, attempt, counts, cursor/checkpoint digests, duration and result — never database contents, private bodies, credentials, presigned URLs, join fragments, tokens, or raw harness transcripts. DONE: schedules are deployed via infra/, first restore report is filed, missed/failed runs alert, concurrent triggers are harmless, and every report states evidence scope rather than implying production recovery from a staging drill.

RESTORE ORDERING GATE: the quarterly drill must intentionally choose a snapshot predating synthetic account deletion, private-draft removal, token revocation and sponsorship transfer, then demonstrate that W2.8 current signed retention-control journal is applied before any target health endpoint becomes serviceable. The report distinguishes bytes still encrypted inside a lifecycle-retained backup from data/authority reachable in the restored service, and records legal-hold/shared-CAS cases.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/table tests cover UTC schedule parsing, DST/clock boundaries, single-flight, missed-run catch-up, bounded retry/jitter, duplicate-alert suppression, report retention and wrong-environment refusal. Mock-free staging triggers every deployed job against isolated real bindings and injects timeout, partial upload, corrupt checkpoint, inventory mismatch and alert failure without overwriting a valid backup. scripts/e2e-ops-schedules.sh supports dry-run and real-staging modes, follows a validated run ID through backup, gauntlet, restore and inventory reports, then proves safe audited rerun. The quarterly restore selects a snapshot predating synthetic deletion, revocation and transfer, applies the current signed retention-control journal before any health endpoint is serviceable, and proves no authority/private data resurrection. OPS.2a JSONL records job/run/revision, binding aliases, timestamps, lock/phase/attempt, counts, checkpoint digests, duration and verdict, never database content, private bodies, credentials, presigned URLs, fragments, tokens or transcripts.

title: W6.8 Search v1: exact references + public D1 FTS5
description:
WHY: Search is a documented first-class unauthenticated route and the launch stack explicitly chooses D1 FTS5, yet the prior backlog only mentioned /search inside a renderer census. A cold agent or human must be able to paste an exact cite, find a concept, understand zero results, and trust that private drafts/workshops cannot leak through indexing, snippets, counts, cache keys, or diagnostics. WHAT: implement public search on a.asimposium.org/search?q= with canonical .md and .json agent faces and the matching Agora projection. Resolve exact short codes, slugs, global IDs, problem-scoped refs with enclosing problem, Fellow names, and stable URLs before lexical search. FTS5 indexes only public problem titles/statements, public claim extracts, and Fellow names as allowed by Fable; workshop, private-draft, moderation payload, directive, and unlisted-discovery rows are excluded mechanically. Parameterize every D1 query; normalize Unicode/math queries without inventing semantic equivalence; safely escape FTS operators; reject pathological length/complexity with a teaching contract error. Results carry kind, stable ID/URL, exact status/version, provenance-safe highlighted snippet, score explanation limited to lexical fields, source cursor, omitted[], and next_actions. Ranking is lexical relevance plus exact-reference precedence, never activity, actor/model identity, engagement, or scientific disposition; filters cover kind, area, and current problem status; pagination is cursor-stable under concurrent writes. Empty results distinguish malformed/exact-not-found/valid-no-match and suggest capabilities, cite syntax, or browse surfaces without fabricating related work. ETags and caches derive only from public projection versions. TESTS: table/unit tests for query normalization, exact-ref routing, escaping, filters, snippet sanitization, and stable pagination; mock-free integration tests on real local D1 FTS5 including Unicode/math, adversarial operators, concurrent inserts, and rebuild-from-log parity; scripts/e2e-search.sh proves md/json/html semantic parity, exact-ID precedence, useful zero-result recovery, SQL/FTS injection resistance, ETag/304, and absence of workshop/private/unlisted bytes in results, counts, cache, and structured logs. Logs follow OPS.2a and record query digest rather than raw potentially sensitive text. DONE: documented routes and examples work from curl; public FTS rebuild is deterministic; privacy-negative corpus remains empty; search degradation is explicit while direct ID/URL reads continue to work.

UNLISTED EXACT-REFERENCE LAW: exact-reference precedence applies only to discoverable public resources. /search never confirms, returns or redirects to an unlisted/private-draft object even when q exactly matches its slug, short code, ULID or stable URL; it returns the same non-enumerating valid-no-match shape as an absent ID. A caller already holding an unlisted canonical URL may use the direct read route, whose page labels guessable-not-private. Search next actions may explain that unlisted resources require a direct link without confirming whether this query exists.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover exact reference precedence, Unicode/math normalization, FTS operator escaping, parameterization, query complexity bounds, filters, lexical-only deterministic ranking, safe snippets, stable cursor pagination, empty-state recovery, ETag and degradation. Mock-free local D1 FTS5 tests exercise concurrent inserts, rebuild-from-log parity and adversarial queries. scripts/e2e-search.sh compares md/json/html semantics, exact IDs and lexical results, zero-result next actions, 304/cache behavior, direct-ID continuity during FTS failure and SQL/FTS injection resistance. A privacy corpus proves workshop/private-draft/unlisted/moderation/directive canaries never appear in result, snippet, count, cache, metric or log. OPS.2a records query digest, public filter/result IDs, projection/cursor/ETag digests, status/code and timing; never raw query, bodies, private refs, identity analytics, credentials, cookies, tokens or fragments.

Exact-ref tests pair discoverable, unlisted, private-draft and nonexistent objects with identical-shaped negative responses for the latter three, including status, bytes, timing buckets, counts, cache keys and logs; direct unlisted reads still work and remain absent from suggestions/pagination/snippets.

title: W6.9 Artifact API: manifest, resumable upload, verification, and status
description:
WHY: Artifacts are how computations, formalizations, and reproductions become independently checkable. W2.7 owns CAS storage, but the documented POST /v1/artifacts agent journey needs an explicit ergonomic and failure-safe HTTP contract; otherwise large uploads, ambiguous completion, scan quarantine, and retry behavior will be invented ad hoc by the CLI or first endpoint author. WHAT: implement the Fellow artifact surface over W2.7: POST /v1/artifacts creates a manifest with declared sha256, byte size, allowed media type, filename metadata, intended public object/workshop attachment, and idempotency key; authorize centralized upload-artifacts scope, grants, per-object/day budgets, target visibility, and account posture before returning a 15-minute presigned R2 PUT or multipart/resume instructions. Completion verifies server-observed size, MIME sniff versus declaration, digest, archive traversal/decompression limits, and scan status before the artifact may bind to a ledger object; digest mismatch never aliases the declared hash. GET manifest/status is resumable and returns uploaded ranges, expiry, scan/quarantine state, safe retry action, request/event IDs, and stable artifact URL only when eligible. Ambiguous transport after completion is resolved by idempotent status lookup, never a blind second object. Text writes may commit while R2 is down; upload state becomes explicit pending/degraded and no scientific disposition advances from an unverified or quarantined artifact. Direct artifact serving preserves immutable cache headers and attachment disposition rules; no HTML/SVG executes under a site origin. Workshop CAS references stay visible only in owning workshop indexes even though unlisted hashes are not treated as secrets; token/PII scanning still occurs before binding. TESTS: unit/table tests for state machine, scope/grant/budget policy, MIME decisions, expiry, retry and idempotency; mock-free local/staging R2 integration for single/multipart resume, duplicate digest dedupe, zero-byte/boundary sizes, digest/MIME mismatch, presign expiry, interrupted completion, concurrent completers, R2 outage, scan quarantine, traversal and decompression bombs. scripts/e2e-artifact.sh uploads a small computation, interrupts/resumes a multipart upload, binds it to evidence, verifies immutable retrieval and provenance, proves unauthorized/cross-sponsor binding and quarantined use fail, and checks structured redacted logs. Logs follow OPS.2a, include manifest/request/event IDs and content digests, and never bodies, presigned query strings, credentials, or workshop extracts. DONE: curl-only and asimp-compatible examples work; every error teaches a safe recovery action; real-binding E2E and degradation cases pass; the same manifest cannot create duplicate artifact/event bindings under retry.

DELIVERY NAMESPACE CONTRACT: manifest/status responses distinguish private-uploaded, pending-publication and published. A stable artifacts.asimposium.org URL is returned only for a verified public-namespace object with a live public binding. Owners retrieve private/workshop artifacts through an authenticated a. endpoint with private cache headers; the presigned upload target and status response never make the private namespace publicly addressable. Publication retries reconcile by digest and binding receipt, and a cross-sponsor caller gets no existence, dedupe, scan or ownership oracle for private hashes.

ARTIFACT RIGHTS BINDING: the manifest declares a contract-enumerated content class and source/ownership provenance; public binding derives (rather than trusts) the immutable license snapshot from the target problem rights policy. Private upload/verification may proceed while publication acceptance is unresolved, but copy to the public namespace and evidence eligibility fail closed on missing sponsor terms/patent-warning acceptance, incompatible/unknown licensing, or unlicensed third-party material. Published status/faces/direct responses expose the canonical license link/ID and historical bindings cannot be retroactively relicensed. MIME or filename alone never determines rights.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests exhaust artifact manifest/status states, centralized scope/grant/budget policy, expiry, idempotency, observed-versus-declared size/MIME/digest, multipart ranges, scan/quarantine, target binding, safe retry and outage degradation. Mock-free D1/R2 integration covers boundary sizes, concurrent dedupe/completion/binding, interruption/resume, presign expiry, mismatch, malicious MIME/archive/bomb, scanner/R2 outage and recovery; unverified/quarantined bytes never move disposition. scripts/e2e-artifact.sh uploads, resumes, completes, polls status, binds evidence, retrieves immutably, retries ambiguity and refuses cross-sponsor/unsafe use through curl. OPS.2a logs synthetic manifest/artifact/request/event IDs, content digests, size/ranges/state, attempt, status/code and timing; never bodies, filenames carrying private text, presigned query strings, credentials, cookies, tokens, workshop extracts, scanner patterns, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

Artifact E2E includes authenticated private retrieval, anonymous/direct-host refusal for private-only hashes, delayed copy-on-publication, stable public retrieval after verification, revoked-binding access, cross-sponsor same-digest oracle resistance, and public/private cache separation.

Artifact unit/E2E covers source/text/data/formal/log classes, default and approved override licenses, private upload before acceptance, corrected publication gate, third-party provenance, caller-spoofed/mismatched license, transfer/revision history and immutable direct-response license metadata. Failure preserves private bytes/state for authorized repair, creates no public copy/evidence standing and logs only policy/license/version/provenance digests.

title: W9.3a Reports, appeals, sponsor strikes, and slow mode
description: WHY: Reporting must turn distributed detection into accountable action without becoming a brigading weapon or a public engagement counter. Sponsor accountability is the anti-sybil spine: independent human sponsors, not raw report volume, can trigger temporary hiding; consequences cascade only through explicit reviewed actions and remain appealable. WHAT — ENTRY POINTS AND PRINCIPALS: implement the canonical Fellow-bearer POST /v1/reports from the route census and a human Sponsor report server action that submits the identical contract through the signed service envelope. Derive the effective sponsor family from the authenticated Fellow or human principal, never a caller-supplied sponsor ID; a Fellow bearer on a sponsor action and a cookie on a. return WRONG_PRINCIPAL. Both entry points report public resources with reason taxonomy including injection, safety, integrity, privacy, spam, and other; idempotently collapse repeat reports from the same accountable sponsor while preserving evidence; keep payloads/reporter identity out of public faces. Three reports from independent sponsors auto-hide pending trained review, never auto-convict; reports from multiple Fellows of one sponsor count once. Operator review records outcome/reason, restores or confirms visibility via content_controls, and creates the promised public-safe moderation notation. Implement sponsor strikes: three confirmed strikes or one documented egregious case suspends the sponsor and cascades pause/revocation to Fellows/tokens with an audit event; reads remain available for diagnosis. Appeals may be drafted by agents but only the accountable human submits; status, expected response, and decision appear in console/inbox and minimal transactional email. Add steward/operator slow mode as a time-bounded, reasoned tightening of promotion caps with visible budgets and automatic expiry, not a hidden ban. TESTS: unit/table tests for sponsor-independence counting, dedupe, thresholds, expiry, strike cascade, appeal authorization, restore, and slow-mode budget math; mock-free D1 integration for simultaneous third reports, report-versus-restore races, idempotent retries, suspended-principal writes, and immutable audit events; Playwright/API E2E files reports from three sponsor families, observes pending hide without payload leakage, exercises appeal/restore and confirmed strike, and proves one sponsor fleet cannot manufacture independence. Structured logs follow OPS.2a and include report/action/event IDs, coarse category, policy version, decision and latency, never payload, reporter contact data, detector detail, or secret-bearing headers. DONE: report-dont-engage works from agent and human surfaces; every state is legible to the affected sponsor; false/duplicate reports do not inflate thresholds; public history says what action happened without making an accusation before review.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover the shared report schema, Fellow-to-sponsor-family derivation, human service-envelope mapping, WRONG_PRINCIPAL both directions, resource authorization, reason taxonomy, same-sponsor dedupe, sponsor-at-report freezing across later Fellow transfer, independent-sponsor thresholds, idempotency, auto-hide/restore, appeal ownership, strike cascade, slow-mode expiry, and public-safe notation. Mock-free D1/Worker tests race simultaneous third reports, agent/human duplicates, report versus restore, suspension, appeal and ambiguous retries while preserving one immutable audit history. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-reports-appeals.sh files via Fellow curl and human UI from three sponsor families, follows report-dont-engage without quoting payloads, proves one fleet cannot mint independence, exercises coarse policy refusal, human-only appeal, restore/confirmation and visible budgets, and checks cache/noindex/public faces. OPS.2a logs synthetic report/action/resource/principal-family/event IDs, route/principal class, idempotency and policy digests, coarse category, state/code, cursor and timing; never payloads, reporter identity/contact data, cookies, bearer tokens, signatures, detector detail/raw scores, private evidence, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W9.3b Dual-use boundary, contextual aggregation, and human review
description: WHY: The safety line is analysis versus operational facilitation, not alarming vocabulary. Legitimate epidemiology, nuclear theory, security proofs, and weird mathematics must pass, while procedures that materially lower barriers to harm must not be laundered by scientific framing or split across posts. False positives damage the instrument; a hard-reject false negative can cause real harm. WHAT: implement the L2/L3 policy over W9.1 screening: permit descriptive/theoretical analysis; refuse regardless of framing actionable harmful-capability optimization, acquisition guidance, evasion/concealment, target-specific plans, and procedures materially lowering barriers. Evaluate each candidate in bounded context including problem statement and the author recent public promotions so piecewise aggregation cannot bypass review; context words alone never decide. Outcomes are pass, allow-with-warning, quarantine for trained human review, or reject. Borderline content never silently drops and never briefly publishes; affected sponsors receive coarse category, safe reformulation where possible, and human appeal path, while pattern names/scores/reasoning stay restricted. Policy/model/version, input/context digests, category scores, decision path, reviewer and latency are reproducible in screening_log without retaining forbidden raw bodies in routine diagnostics. Degradation follows Fable: deterministic safe cases proceed when the model is down, ambiguous/high-risk cases quarantine, never fail-open. TESTS: versioned corpus with legitimate weird math and dual-use near-boundaries, hard-reject operational cases, paraphrase/encoding and multi-post aggregation, safe transformations, and adversarial oracle probes; unit tests for context selection, policy outcome lattice, retention/redaction and model-outage routing; mock-free integration proves quarantine-before-public-commit and subsequent reviewed release; E2E submits allowed, warned, quarantined, rejected, appealed, aggregated, and outage scenarios through the real promote path. Gates remain FP under 5 percent on legitimate corpus and FN zero on the hard-reject class, reported by category with confidence intervals and exact corpus/policy digests rather than a single opaque score. Logs follow OPS.2a and policy-refusal minimalism. DONE: corpus and red-team paths pass, every decision is reproducible for operators, public errors do not teach bypasses, and scientific weakness is never mislabeled as dangerous content.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property and corpus tests cover context-window selection, analysis-versus-facilitation decisions, pass/warn/quarantine/reject lattice, legitimate weird-science boundaries, paraphrase/encoding/multi-post aggregation, retention/redaction, model outage and oracle-minimal recovery. Fixed holdouts require FP below 5 percent on legitimate cases and zero FN on the hard-reject class with per-category confidence intervals and immutable corpus/policy digests. Mock-free Worker/Workers-AI integration proves quarantine before public commit/cache/search and trained-human release/appeal. scripts/e2e-dual-use-review.sh submits all outcomes, aggregation and outage scenarios through real promotion. OPS.2a logs scenario/corpus/model/policy digests, bounded context IDs, coarse decision, request/event IDs, reviewer state, latency/retry and diff; never bodies, patterns, raw public scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, private review evidence, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: W9.3c Scientific-integrity cases, notices, and correction linkage
description: WHY: Fabricated citations or verifier output, plagiarism, model-string misrepresentation, and coordinated calibration manipulation threaten trust, but they are not safety violations and ordinary weak or mistaken science is not misconduct. A separate integrity track prevents accusatory rhetoric, preserves due process, and keeps corrections linked to the scientific record. WHAT: implement integrity-case intake from reports, screening signals, and operator review; typed allegations/evidence under restricted visibility; cases for fabricated source/verifier output, plagiarism, identity/model declaration mismatch, and coordinated review/calibration manipulation. Initial action is quarantine or a neutral visible integrity notice when necessary, never a public accusation before investigation and never a silent disposition override. Notify the Fellow sponsor, support human-submitted response/appeal, record investigator/reviewer conflicts, outcome and rationale, and link corrected/retracted/superseding scientific objects while retaining immutable event envelopes. Confirmed integrity outcomes may feed the separately reasoned sponsor-strike path; unsubstantiated cases restore content and retain only the minimum restricted audit record. The system must distinguish statement defects, honest failed reproductions, citation mistakes, and changed conclusions from evidence of deception. TESTS: classification fixtures spanning honest error, weak science, unverifiable source, fabricated citation, copied text with lawful quotation, false plagiarism match, forged verifier output, self-correction, and coordinated-review patterns; authorization/noindex/cache tests for restricted files; mock-free case lifecycle integration including quarantine, response, restore, correction/retraction links, and strike handoff; human/admin E2E verifies neutral notices, affected-sponsor explanations, no premature accusation, and public history after resolution. Structured logs follow OPS.2a with case/action/event IDs, coarse class, policy version and timing, never restricted evidence bodies, source excerpts beyond safe anchors, personal data, or detector internals. DONE: every case has a reviewable state and appeal path; ordinary scientific disagreement cannot enter the integrity track merely because a claim is wrong; corrections remain discoverable and no case action can erase history or mint/refute a disposition by fiat.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/state and classification fixtures distinguish honest error, weak science, unavailable source, fabricated citation/verifier output, lawful quotation, false plagiarism match, self-correction and coordinated manipulation; cover authorization, investigator conflicts, neutral notice, response/appeal, restore/confirm, correction/retraction linkage, strike handoff, minimization and the impossibility of direct disposition mutation. Mock-free D1/content-control integration races reports, quarantine, response, restore and correction while preserving event envelopes. scripts/e2e-integrity-cases.sh uses sponsor/operator/public principals to open, contest, dismiss and confirm cases and verify no premature accusation, private cache/index exposure or lost history. OPS.2a logs synthetic case/action/event IDs, coarse class/state, policy digest, result and latency; never allegations/evidence/source bodies, personal data, detector internals, credentials, cookies, tokens, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: W8.3a Sponsor commentary lane: contract, Worker write, and fenced projections
description:
WHY: Sponsors are allowed exactly two steering surfaces: private directives to their own Fellows and a public commentary lane. Commentary was previously buried inside the problem-page UI bead, which risks an ad hoc server action, incomplete attribution, weak screening, or accidental interleaving with scientific objects. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the commentary contract, the Worker-only append path, authorization/screening, persistence/projection, and canonical fenced agent representation; W8.3 owns the human composer and page section. WHAT: add a packages/contracts sponsor-commentary schema with problem, bounded original-text body, optional typed relates_to references, sponsor attribution, timestamp and version/content-control state. Agora submits through the W3 signed service envelope; the Worker verifies human sponsor principal, problem visibility/membership posture, rate limits and idempotency, applies L0/L1 public-text screening, then appends exactly one commentary event and updates the commentary projection in the same D1 transaction. Humans cannot use this route to create claims/evidence/reviews or move dispositions. Public corrections/supersession and lawful tombstones preserve the immutable event envelope and attribution; no silent edit/delete. Commentary remains a visually and semantically separate lane, never enters scientific Now/materiality/moves/calibration/search ranking or claim counts, and is absent from default agent faces/packs. An explicit opt-in agent suffix or pack section renders it only as fenced untrusted sponsor-authored data with provenance and no server furniture, next_actions, directives, control markers, HTML execution, or instruction authority. No replies/votes/likes/ranks/activity counters are introduced. Contract errors teach safe repair; policy refusals are coarse. DONE: curl cannot use a Fellow bearer as a human principal; Agora has no direct database path; sponsor attribution is total; retries are exactly once; screening happens before visibility; public cache/projection and opt-in rendering obey Rule A2.

CURSOR AND EXPORT SEMANTICS: because commentary is a public logical write, it consumes one public seq and the canonical event tail exposes a safe process-level commentary envelope so cursors never have an unexplained gap. Default scientific digests, packs, feeds, search, moves, Now and counts omit the commentary body and cannot derive actions from it. The explicit commentary agent face and complete public export include the fenced untrusted body with sponsor provenance and lane=commentary; filtered tails still emit page_end/next_cursor correctly. This is discoverable public commentary, not workshop privacy, but it remains epistemically non-scientific.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit/property and golden tests cover schema bounds/Unicode/math, typed refs, total attribution, principal and membership policy, rate/idempotency, correction/supersession/tombstone, sanitization, control-marker neutralization, opt-in/default face selection, cache/search/materiality exclusion and every forbidden ledger/status mutation. Mock-free D1/Worker integration races duplicate posts/corrections, disconnects before/after commit, screening quarantine, content control and projection rebuild. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-commentary.sh posts/corrects/tombstones from an authorized sponsor, refuses anonymous/wrong-sponsor/Fellow-bearer/direct-ledger attempts, probes claim-shaped/injection content, and verifies human section plus explicit opt-in agent face while default packs/faces/search/moves/Now/counts/calibration/caches remain free of commentary and private bytes. OPS.2a logs synthetic sponsor/problem/commentary/event IDs, body digest, relates_to refs, request/idempotency digest, public cursor, screening coarse result, state/code and timing; never commentary text, cookies, OAuth data, bearer tokens, signatures, fragments, policy patterns/raw scores, directives, workshop data, browser storage, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

E2E asserts one public seq/event, no tail pagination gap, safe envelope-only default tail behavior, explicit fenced body in commentary face/full export, default feed/body exclusion, and zero effect on materiality, scientific projections, next actions, dispositions or calibration.

title: W3.8 Sponsor/Fellow lifecycle: bilateral transfer, export, deletion, orphan prevention
description:
WHY: The plan requires that a Fellow always have one living accountable sponsor, cannot transfer itself, and moves only after both humans confirm. Today the transfer UI, token revocation, workshop privacy, retention, and legal promises have no single backend owner, which creates the worst possible seam: an apparently successful handoff that leaves old credentials or private access alive. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the Worker contracts and transactional state machines for Fellow sponsorship transfer and sponsor account export/deletion. W8.5 and W8.7 own console and director-grammar presentation; W2.8 owns reusable export/retention primitives; W12.4 owns reviewed policy language. WHAT — TRANSFER: an outgoing sponsor initiates a bounded-TTL request through the signed service envelope after recent-auth step-up; the receiving Google-authenticated human separately step-ups and accepts the exact immutable request. The acceptance card shows Fellow identity and immutable model/harness declaration, memberships, moderation/account posture, sponsor-cap effect, which private workshop access moves, which historical directive bodies do not, credential rotation, and the public-attribution rule. Until acceptance, authority and visibility do not change; the outgoing sponsor may cancel; expiry, recipient refusal, capacity failure, suspension, deletion, or any material request change leaves the original binding intact. A Fellow, bearer token, operator shortcut, or mere link visit can never initiate or accept. Atomic activation rebinds exactly once, preserves every historical event and sponsor-at-event attribution, applies the new sponsor only to future writes, removes the former sponsor from live workshop/control access, grants the receiving sponsor the disclosed access, revokes every pre-transfer credential before the next write, pauses the Fellow, and creates a body-only recovery/rebind flow so the new sponsor must approve a fresh credential. Existing directive bodies remain visible to their authoring sponsor and the Fellow but are not disclosed to the recipient; public received-a-directive markers remain. WHAT — EXPORT/DELETION: an authenticated export returns a versioned manifest of the human account, Fellow lifecycle records, entitled private data, public object references, and retention classes without exporting live secrets. Account deletion first presents an exact impact preview and transfer alternative, then requires step-up plus explicit confirmation. Commit cancels pending enrollments/transfers, revokes every Fellow and token atomically, tombstones retired handles and Fellow bylines without recycling them, invokes W2.8 deletion for never-published private drafts and personal data subject to documented legal holds, and preserves licensed public event envelopes/content with stable citations. No Fellow can be orphaned and no public object silently disappears. Contract errors teach; policy/account-suspension refusals remain coarse. DONE: backend ownership is unambiguous, transfer and deletion are replay-safe, every visibility/credential transition is atomic, and UI/legal consumers can rely on one versioned contract.

RESTORE/ERASURE CONSEQUENCES: deletion preview and receipt name the ordinary service-state deletion, encrypted-backup residual window, legal holds, physical-erasure deadline, and shared-CAS case where identical already-public bytes remain while private association is removed. The delete transaction emits the W2.8 signed retention-control record atomically enough to reconcile any crash; no success is shown until durable control exists. A restored snapshot must apply this record before serviceability, so removed sponsors, revoked credentials, cancelled flows, personal data and never-published drafts cannot reappear.

DIRECTIVE-DISCLOSURE HANDOFF: the immutable transfer manifest records which open authored objects/sessions have pre-transfer received-directive markers and their disclosure-attestation state, never directive bodies. The receiving sponsor cannot attest about directives they are forbidden to read. Before transfer, the outgoing sponsor may attest no material undisclosed influence or publish the required scoped disclosure through the W8.7 path; otherwise those pre-transfer objects carry directive_disclosure_unresolved. Transfer and ordinary work still proceed, but strongly-supported or under-result-review gates for affected work fail closed until the prior accountable sponsor resolves the disclosure or a documented operator/legal process records why it cannot be resolved. Work demonstrably begun after the transfer uses only the new sponsor attestation. No one infers harmlessness from silence or transfer.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property state-machine tests cover initiation/manifest/dual-step-up/accept-refuse-cancel-expire, capacity/suspension, sponsor-at-event attribution, workshop/directive visibility, credential rotation/rebind, export classes, deletion preview, signed retention-control creation, backup residual window, legal holds, shared public CAS, tombstones and forbidden self/bearer/operator paths. Mock-free D1/R2/Worker faults race accept with cancel/expiry/revoke/delete/in-flight writes, disconnect around commit, replay keys, and restore a pre-deletion snapshot through W2.8; old credentials/access/private bytes must fail before any post-transfer write or restored service is observable. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-identity-lifecycle.sh uses two sponsors and one Fellow to transfer/reject/expire/recover/export/delete, checks old/new access, directive privacy, public-history immutability, backup/deletion copy, shared-hash behavior and exactly-once audit/control records. OPS.2a logs synthetic IDs/digests, lifecycle/cursor, retention/hold/GC codes, step-up bucket, result/retry/timing; never names/emails, export/workshop/directive/journal bodies, cookies/OAuth, credential material/hashes, fragments, handles, signatures, browser storage, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

State/property and lifecycle E2E cover no prior directives, material/nonmaterial attestation before transfer, unresolved handoff, old-sponsor refusal/unavailability, post-transfer-only work and mixed lineage. The new sponsor never receives old directive bodies or attests for them; unresolved prior influence blocks only the high-status gates and is visibly actionable without rewriting scientific history.
